a06d4d2e1761844d: FRANKFURT, Germany: A flight from a Greek holiday island to Germany accidentally sent out a hijacking alert to several European countries Tuesday, prompting fighter jets to be scrambled and a brief airport closure.
The service operated by Corendon Airlines was en route from Corfu to Nuremberg in southern Germany when it "inadvertently" transmitted the alert, German police said.
"The aircraft could no longer be reached by radio to clarify the situation," prompting warnings to be activated in several European countries, police said.
A Rafale fighter jet was scrambled from Croatia to intercept the Boeing passenger jet while the German military also dispatched warplanes.
Nuremberg airport suspended operations after the alert was triggered and police were deployed to the scene.
But after the German fighter jets escorted the plane to land, police inspected the aircraft and found there was no danger.
In the early hours Tuesday, flights were also briefly disrupted at the airport after pilots reported suspected drone sightings.
Several German airports have had to suspend operations for brief periods in recent months due to drone activity, with suspicion often falling on Russia.
Germany, one of Ukraine's key backers in its fight against Russia, accuses Moscow of waging a campaign of espionage and sabotage on its soil.
9e67338383fe9d84: If you’re looking for an e-reader that can easily fit in your pocket (or snap onto your magnet-equipped phone), the tiny Xteink X4 Pro might be worth a look. It features a 4.26-inch, 800 x 480 E Ink display, making it significantly smaller and thinner than Amazon’s smallest six-inch Kindle. It’s also quite a bit cheaper. Right now, you can pick it up for $84.15 ($25 off) at Amazon, which is its best price to date.

The X4 Pro brings several welcome upgrades over its predecessors, including a touchscreen that gives readers another way to interact with it. It still has physical page-turning buttons, though. There’s also a new touch-sensitive button below the display for quickly returning to the home screen, along with a built-in light with adjustable brightness and color temperature, so you can read in the dark. It ships with the excellent CrossPoint Reader software, which makes navigating your library and reading books a much better experience than on previous Xteink models we’ve tested, though it’s still not quite as polished as Amazon’s software.

Understandably, not everyone is a fan of Xteink’s decision to swap the X4 Pro’s USB-C port for a proprietary charging connector. If you can look past that, the X4 Pro is a great, little e-reader that features magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones, just like previous models. The magnetic connection is stronger this time around, though we still wish it were a little more secure. All the same, my colleague Andrew Liszewski still considers the X4 Pro the best tiny e-reader you can buy, calling it a device he “won’t leave the house without.”

12771f19d7ef292b: Zverev defies 'physical issues' to reach Shanghai Masters quarter-finals
AFP

SHANGHAI: Top-seeded Alexander Zverev toughed out two tie-breaks to beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (8/6), 4-6, 7-6 (7/1) at the Shanghai Masters on Tuesday, winning his first match since being guaranteed the year-end world number one ranking.
The 29-year-old German will play Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals.
"Really difficult match," Zverev said.
"I had some physical issues so, you know, I was maybe slower," he told the crowd.
"My ankle was acting up unfortunately again," Zverev elaborated in an on-court interview, later adding that his decline started in the second set.
"I'm starting to feel my body more, but happy to be through."
Zverev, the current world number two, was guaranteed the year-end number one spot after third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz lost to Zizou Bergs in Shanghai on Monday.
On Tuesday, Zverev called the honour "special", saying it was a different feeling to winning tournaments, adding he was "looking forward" to the responsibility of owning that status.
Neither player could create much trouble for his opponent in the first set as they traded aces to hold serve.
But Zverev found himself under pressure when he was forced to save a set point before making it into a tie-break.
He kept his composure as Bublik squandered three set points in a row, taking the first set with a commanding forehand at the net.

That momentum was cut short when Bublik broke the German's serve in the fifth game of the second set. Despite a few clutch backhands a sombre-looking Zverev was unable to avoid tumbling into a deciding third.
The players soon found themselves staring down another tie-break, but this time Zverev raced to a 6-1 lead and closed out the match with an ace.
- Gea goes on -
Earlier, 56th-ranked Arthur Gea put on a convincing show to beat Jakub Mensik 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 in their fourth-round encounter.

Mensik, ranked 15th, hit the ground trying to convert a crucial break point in the final minutes of the second set, but Gea got past his opponent with a cross-court backhand and won on his first match point.
"I'm enjoying how I'm playing. I feel I'm improving all the time," said Gea, the lowest-ranked player left in the draw.
Asked if he might recreate last year's "miracle" that saw Valentin Vacherot claim the title as world number 204, Gea said he would "see what happens."
"I don't think it's miracle when you work hard every day, but I hope to do the same," he said.
Two days earlier the 21-year-old Frenchman beat US Open finalist Ben Shelton, the third seed, 7-6 (7/5), 7-6 (7/3) in the third round for the biggest victory of his career.
Gea next faces Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who reached the quarter-finals after beating Hubert Hurkacz 1-6, 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) in a dramatic tie-break.
Davidovich Fokina, ranked 26th, beat the 2023 Shanghai champion at the third time of asking after blundering a smash and diving to the ground for a point in vain.

f09456b1b5be8629: LONDON: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery wants his side to get back to winning ways on home turf when they face Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The Birmingham club's form at Villa Park has been one of the key factors in Villa's rise up the Premier League table, with the 1982 European champions now competing again in the continent's top club competition for the second time in three years.
But Villa have yet to win at home this season, with two defeats and a draw from three games.

One factor in the slump may be the fact that they are playing in front of a reduced crowd at Villa Park, with the North Stand out of action while it is refurbished for Euro 2028 and the ground as a whole something of a building site.
But Emery believes the game against Turkish club Fenerbahce offers an opportunity for a reset.
"We are realistic about how we are working and improving things," Emery told a press conference on Tuesday.
"But it is not enough yet, so we are having lots of conversations with the team, in meetings and with videos, practising too to show improvements in matches.

"At Villa Park, we have not won yet, so it is very important how we can improve things to be closer to winning. Tomorrow is a very good opportunity to do one step forward in those improvements and the players as well to get confidence and feel comfortable."

The Spaniard added: "Villa Park is for us something very, very special. It should be like the four years that we are here – how we achieved this as a special place, our fortress. Tomorrow is a new challenge to show it."

Villa's start to the season has been hampered by injuries and they have suffered another blow in the build-up to the second round of Champions League fixtures, with Italian defender Matteo Ruggeri set to be sidelined for a month because of a hamstring problem after coming at half-time during last weekend's 2-2 draw with Brentford.
"Ruggeri, we don't know exactly how long it's going to be, but it will be some weeks that he's going to be out, more than one month," said Emery.
"We need to find solutions because (Ian) Maatsen is not yet available."

1f62d11b47df3600: A financial analyst is questioning whether the collapse in AI costs owing to the arrival of Chinese, low-cost and open source models will cause a “reset” in the AI story as cloud providers struggle to recoup trillions of dollars of capital spending. In a recent research note focused on Asian markets, Jefferies estimates that about half of the roughly $2.3 trillion contracted backlog at Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle is owned by OpenAI and Anthropic. Yet Chinese AI models, open source/weight and small language models, threaten to undercut the prices the two US leaders charge, casting doubt on their future revenue. Jefferies points to research from global aggregator platform OpenRouter, which found Chinese models processed 76.12 trillion tokens in the week ended 27 September, up from just 4.37 trillion in late April. The top four US providers processed 14.2 trillion tokens. Meanwhile, the launch of Moonshot AI’s open source Kimi K3 is “competing at the frontier” with an estimated 95 percent of the performance of Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5. “The question now is whether all of the above has been priced fully into markets. This writer does not think so,” the Jefferies paper states. The largest hyperscalers are set to collectively spend between $600 and $800 billion this year on building datacenters, funding it increasingly with debt rather than cash. Jefferies, however, questions where the hyperscalers' future revenue streams will come from. “It can no longer be assumed, most particularly with the arrival of the likes of Kimi K3, that large language models will ever be profitable given the related ongoing collapse in token pricing. This is extremely relevant for the hyperscalers since they have invested in datacenter capacity on the assumption that the compute will be purchased by the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI,” the paper says. While the long term bet on AI may be sound, in the medium term, there is a lot of uncertainty, it argues. “The AI story will be due for a big reset at some point in the not-so-distant future. Are the four hyperscalers really going to spend $993 billion on capex in 2027?” Jefferies questions. There are also important questions to ask about how much of the hyperscalers’ reported profits are down to their investments in AI model builders on which they will also depend for revenue. “Other income and expenses” — which describes gains in investments — have spiked in importance. Jefferies says these investments are “likely to include positions in unlisted AI-related stocks.” While the four major hyperscalers’ annualized earnings increased by $222 billion to reach $581 billion in the four quarters to 2Q26, “other non-operating income/loss” accounted for all of that increase, according to the analyst. Jefferies says “other non-operating income/loss” increased by $224 billion year-on-year to $237 billion over the same period, meaning it accounted "for all of the increase in earnings." Other research has underlined how much revenue and borrowing cloud providers might need to fund their datacenter building plans. The 2026 annual Global Technology Report from management consultants Bain & Company says the AI industry must generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to keep funding the infrastructure needed to meet anticipated demand. That means the industry will need new uses beyond employee productivity. Bain suspects existing AI applications might make up $1.8 trillion in revenue, but this still leaves a $4.2 trillion shortfall. It could be plugged by emerging AI applications such as search engines and ads, AI-built autonomous vehicles, and AI simulations. Even if they work out, these new categories will only add up to $1.5 trillion in revenue, leaving a $2.7 trillion gap which might be filled by “new products and uses that don’t exist today.” The Register does not offer investment advice.®

55737792ab3956a3: KUALA LUMPUR: The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) generated an economic impact of nearly RM950 million, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the race, held from Oct 2 to 4, attracted approximately 261,000 fans, including an estimated 103,000 on race day.
Citing Formula One Management (FOM), he said the race was broadcast internationally and watched by 827 million viewers.
"More than 97,000 tickets were estimated to have been sold, while more than 50,000 international tourists and about 5,000 foreign workers came to Malaysia for the event," he said.
Taufiq said the event was made possible through close cooperation between SIC and Bahrain International Circuit, with support from the government and other stakeholders.

He said the arrival of international spectators also benefited the tourism, hospitality, aviation and small and medium-sized enterprise sectors, while promoting Malaysia as a sporting and investment destination.
Unlike previous arrangements, Bahrain bore the hosting rights costs, allowing Malaysia to benefit economically from the event, he said.
SIC and an appointed consultancy firm would conduct a cost-benefit assessment, as the race had only recently concluded.
"The findings of the cost-benefit assessment will be among the considerations for the government in determining whether Malaysia should consider hosting Formula 1 again in the future," he said.

He was responding to Rodiyah Sapiee (Batang Sadong), who asked about the race's economic benefits compared with government costs and whether a cost-benefit assessment would guide future decisions on hosting F1 regularly.

8e96da25eca0d54f: KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly 14 million Malaysians have benefited from subsidised RON95 petrol under the Budi95 scheme, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the figure, recorded as at Sept 30, represented about 85 per cent of the more than 16.5 million eligible Malaysians.
Anwar said beneficiaries could buy RON95 petrol at RM1.99 a litre by verifying their identity through MyKad, in a written parliamentary reply to Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman (PN-Bachok).
He said the government's latest assessment showed positive results in improving subsidy targeting, reducing leakage and protecting consumers' purchasing power.
The shift from blanket to targeted subsidies meant the benefits were no longer widely enjoyed by ineligible groups, including foreigners, he said.
The scheme is projected to generate annual savings of between RM2.5 billion and RM4 billion, depending on global crude oil prices, exchange rates and actual fuel consumption.
Anwar said the additional fiscal space would allow the government to strengthen assistance programmes, including Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah.

Eligible e-hailing drivers were provided with additional fuel entitlements of up to 800 litres a month, based on actual travel distances verified through data supplied by e-hailing operators, he said.
The government would continue reviewing Budi95 based on actual consumption, global energy prices and the country's fiscal position, he added.
3ddaf3b9d433bd59: SEOUL: South Korean police said they had detained a man suspected of stabbing eight people on Tuesday at a shopping mall in the city of Incheon, and the Yonhap news agency said one of the victims was in a life-threatening condition.
Officers are investigating the motive and circumstances of the attack, a police spokesperson said by telephone.

A witness cited by Yonhap said the suspect appeared to have knives tied to both hands and moved through several floors of the shopping mall, attacking people as he went before being subdued by bystanders and handed over to police.
President Lee Jae Myung urged a swift and rigorous investigation after visiting the Incheon Metropolitan Police Agency and being briefed on the case, according to his office.
"I pray for a swift recovery of those who were harmed in today's stabbing rampage incident," Lee said in an X post.

Yonhap said the 59-year-old suspect had previously served a four-year prison sentence for attempted murder.

The suspect has been fitted with an electronic monitoring ankle bracelet since his release in 2019, and had been receiving treatment for mental health issues and alcohol addiction, the Justice Ministry said in a statement.
The electronic monitoring system is a crime prevention programme that covers people convicted of a range of crimes including murder.
The ministry pledged to conduct a thorough investigation of the system, which uses real-time GPS tracking to monitor high-risk offenders after their release from prison.
Incheon, west of Seoul, is home to South Korea's main airport and forms part of the wider Seoul metropolitan area.
South Korea was shaken by a series of stabbing rampages in 2023, including attacks that left multiple people dead and injured.

38173097bce9c6a6: PETALING JAYA: Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders do not need to pass Bahasa Melayu to qualify for Sarawak’s Free Tertiary Education Scheme (FTES), says Sarawak’s deputy minister of education, innovation and talent development Dr Annuar Rapaee.

He said eligibility depended on meeting the academic and programme-specific admission requirements of the four participating institutions – Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus, University of Technology Sarawak (UTS), Curtin University Malaysia and i-CATS University College.

According to The Borneo Post, he said UEC holders did not need to pass Bahasa Melayu to qualify for admission. However, he said they should be proficient in English as it is the main language of instruction at the four institutions.

“They do not need Bahasa Melayu to qualify for entry into our four universities or to receive free tertiary education,” he said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak state assembly sitting.
He was responding to See Chee How (Independent-Batu Lintang) about the eligibility criteria for UEC holders under FTES.

Annuar said admission requirements varied by institution and programme A UEC holder generally needs five Grade Bs to qualify for a bachelor’s degree programme, along with additional prerequisite subjects for certain courses such as Mathematics, Additional Mathematics and Physical Science. Some institutions also imposed their own English-language proficiency requirements.
UEC holders admitted to any of the 64 courses covered by FTES would not need to submit a separate application for the scheme.

As of June 30, 192 UEC students were receiving full tuition fee coverage under FTES. Of these, 137 were studying at Swinburne Sarawak, 33 at UTS, 21 at Curtin Malaysia and one at i-CATS University College.
Annuar said UEC students would receive the same treatment as other students in securing industrial placements, provided they obtained placements in the relevant industries.

He said the inclusion of UEC holders in FTES reflected Sarawak’s policy of ensuring that deserving Sarawakians had equal opportunities to pursue higher education and develop their potential, skills and talents.

He added that Sarawak’s education policy was based on the principle that education should transcend race and ethnicity, serve as a means of social mobility, and help lift communities out of poverty – particularly in rural areas.
“No deserving Sarawakian should be denied educational opportunities,” he said.
“I hope this sends a very clear message to all Sarawakians, particularly UEC holders, that you are no different from others.”

The UEC is the school-leaving certificate for students attending Chinese independent schools and is academically equivalent to the national Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) or international A-levels.
The certificate was recognised by Sarawak in 2016 for entry to state civil service positions, state-owned colleges and universities, and to qualify for Yayasan Sarawak education loans.

ade3e882989d9c39: Asian refiners look set to be among the biggest beneficiaries of a sustained recovery in Middle Eastern crude oil exports.
Oil exports from the Middle East have largely returned to pre-war levels as tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz have increased.

Total crude oil and condensate exports from the region — excluding Iran — averaged 18.11 million tonnes a week last month, according to Kpler, compared with a weekly average of around 18.22 million tonnes during the eight weeks prior to the start of the conflict with Iran at the end of February.
However, Middle Eastern fuel exports remain at less than half of pre-war levels due to damage to regional refineries.

That gap works in favour of those who can fill it. Asia holds around 37 per cent of global refining capacity, according to the Energy Institute, and refiners in India, China, South Korea and Singapore are well placed to capture the value attached to turning crude into petrol, diesel and jet fuel.
The gains are not Asia's alone, as refining margins have climbed in all regions this year because fuel prices have risen more than crude oil costs.

Even so, the recovery in Middle Eastern oil supplies should mean that a larger share of the profits and pricing power attached to those barrels will flow to Asia's refining hubs for as long as the Gulf's own refineries remain impaired.

Before the war, Gulf producers spent years expanding downstream. Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates invested heavily in refining and petrochemical capacity, seeking to capture more value from each barrel and reduce reliance on crude exports alone.

The conflict with Iran has disrupted that strategy. Roughly 20 refineries across the Middle East have been struck since fighting began, taking more than 2.3 million barrels per day (bpd) of refining capacity offline.

Damage assessments have been slow because of continuing tensions, but refineries are among the most complex industrial facilities in the energy sector and are much more difficult to repair than oil wells.
That situation means crude output and exports are likely to recover well before refining capacity does, leaving oil producers in the Middle East to rely on other refiners to process their crude.
Asian refineries have cut utilisation rates notably since the conflict began as crude supplies collapsed and shipping costs surged.

The Middle East supplied around 60 per cent of Asia's crude imports last year, according to Kpler, and the sudden drop in flows from the region prompted refiners across Asia to slash throughput by six million bpd in April, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).

Refinery output has crept higher since, but there's room for further expansion. Many of Asia's large coastal complexes were built specifically to import crude in bulk and convert it into fuels and petrochemicals for domestic and export markets.
India appears particularly well positioned to benefit.

The country sits less than four days by sea from the Gulf's major export terminals and is close to fuel-hungry markets across South and Southeast Asia that have faced supply disruptions since the conflict began.
China also stands to gain. It possesses the world's largest refining system, with capacity of around 18.8 million bpd.
South Korea and Singapore could benefit from higher utilisation rates and increased export activity.
As more crude is routed through Asian processing hubs, those centres become increasingly important to global fuel security, pricing and trade flows.
The broader significance of recovering Gulf production may ultimately be a shift in where influence is exercised across oil markets.
Just over one-third of global crude oil and condensate exports came from the Americas during the second quarter of this year, according to data from Kpler.
That figure compares with an average of roughly 22 per cent since 2024.
The shift has given the United States and other regional producers greater influence over trade flows, pricing dynamics and energy security discussions.
A sustained return of Middle Eastern crude would alter that balance.
A decade ago, Gulf producers set out to capture more value from every barrel by expanding into refining and fuel exports.
The war has pushed them back down the value chain, at least for now. Until they rebuild what was damaged, much of the value in Gulf crude is likely to be captured further east.

a2352b9071f96ed2: When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. Ramanan berkata, kementerian menerusi Talent Corporation Malaysia Bhd (TalentCorp) telah mengenal pasti 12 skop kerja pekerjaan berpermintaan tinggi dalam sektor pusat data, yang mana sebahagian besar memerlukan kemahiran teknikal khusus.

Ia termasuk jurutera elektrik, jurutera mekanikal, pengurus projek (IT), jurutera pentauliahan, arkitek penyelesaian, jurutera keselamatan rangkaian, pengurus fasiliti, juruteknik pusat data, juruteknik fasiliti, dan chargeman.

Daripada 12 peranan tersebut, lapan memerlukan Ijazah, satu memerlukan diploma, dua memerlukan kelulusan pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET), dan satu (chargeman) memerlukan Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) beserta sijil kekompetenan Suruhanjaya Tenaga.
Ramanan berkata, ini menunjukkan sektor tersebut menawarkan peluang kerja kepada graduan universiti dan graduan institusi TVET.
Malaysia mempunyai 125 pusat data dengan kapasiti aktif 925.6MW, manakala 2GW lagi dalam pembinaan dan 3.1GW dalam perancangan, memetik laporan syarikat penyelidikan BMI.
Meskipun berdepan persaingan yang semakin meningkat daripada Vietnam dan Thailand, BMI menjangkakan Malaysia akan kekal sebagai pasaran pusat data teraju Asia Tenggara.
Namun, timbul kebimbangan yang dilaporkan secara meluas menyatakan lonjakan pelaburan pusat data di Malaysia boleh memberi tekanan kepada bekalan air dan elektrik.

bf6c30932fdce6aa: Winston Peters, the veteran leader of New Zealand First, has borrowed heavily from the culture-war playbook that has energised populist parties across the English-speaking world, railing against "woke" politics, gender policy and high immigration ahead of next month's general election.
So far, political analysts say, the pay-off has been limited.

While the right has surged in countries such as Britain and Australia and Donald Trump's "Make America Great Again" (MAGA) platform secured him a second presidential term, Peters' decades-old New Zealand First remains a smaller force, even as it sharpens its message ahead of the country's Nov 7 vote.

Peters is betting that frustration over immigration, cost-of-living pressures and debates over national identity, gender and abortion can push his party to a stronger result and make it indispensable to Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right bloc.
But some analysts say the same rhetoric that has resonated abroad is running into a more secular, less polarised electorate at home.

Given current tight polling and New Zealand's proportional representation voting system, Luxon's National Party will need the seats of New Zealand First and the right-wing ACT party for a chance to form the government again and keep the country on its conservative track.

"This time it's almost now or never in terms of getting far greater power to implement our alternative to how to run an economy," said Peters, 81, arguing voters had previously given New Zealand First only limited power.
Grant Welman, who runs a handyman business, said the crowd at a Peters event in Tauranga was made up of "everyday Kiwis" with "a deep concern for the direction of the country".
"I am voting New Zealand First this election, not because I believe they're the greatest, but I do believe that they are the best choice available."

Founded in 1993, New Zealand First has long combined social conservatism on issues such as immigration and Indigenous rights, with an interventionist economic programme that includes stronger state support for the elderly and regional development.
Peters has played a pivotal role in coalition-building, helping form four of the past 10 governments and serving as foreign minister in three.
This time around, he has ruled out a coalition with the centre-left Labour Party.
But Peters faces a new challenger to his role as kingmaker with the emergence of the centrist Opportunity party, which could hold the balance of power after the election.
It supports immigration, policies on LGBT rights and enhanced environmental protections.
Peters — who rejects the populist label, saying all politicians want to be popular — has framed his attacks on "woke" politics as a defence of common sense, experience and national sovereignty.
New Zealand First has sponsored a bill to define "woman" and "man" in law, has proposed immigration curbs and advocates leaving the Paris climate accord.
"The 2026 campaign is the most explicitly right-wing pitch NZ First has made in its 33-year history," said Josh Van Veen, a politics academic and former New Zealand First staffer.
"This might well be inspired by a global populist movement, but the polling would suggest it doesn't have quite the same appeal it does elsewhere in the Anglosphere."
New Zealand First won 6.1 per cent of the vote in 2023 and rose as high as 13.6 per cent in an April poll.
But recent surveys suggest that momentum has faded, putting the party's support around 10 per cent.
By contrast, Pauline Hanson's One Nation is nudging 30 per cent support in Australia, while Reform UK is at about 23.4 per cent in British polling averages.

"There just isn't a big constituency for the kind of MAGA-style politics that Peters and (NZ First lawmaker Shane) Jones sometimes lean into," said Van Veen, pointing to a recent 29-country survey that found New Zealanders the most open to immigration.

Ben Thomas, a political commentator, said New Zealand was somewhat insulated from the culture wars because its proportional voting system did provide a "release valve for those views" and stopped them infiltrating the major parties as has been the case in the United States.
"It would be nice to think about New Zealanders as sort of rough-hewn, earthy common sense, which leaves them somewhat inoculated from those kind of global forces," he said.

b0ce7e8ccbd20243: MALAYSIAN public spaces and homes are so laden with prized assets and objects that they constantly attract thieves who steal and fence valuables with ease.
Besides targeting cars and motorcycles to strip for components, thieves burglarise homes for cash, jewellery, electrical and electronic appliances like laptops and smartphones. That's not all.
They also steal durian — the expensive musang king variety especially — from unprotected orchards, and rustle cattle ahead of major festive seasons when demand for meat spikes.
Years ago, thieves favoured steel manhole covers and brass water meters from residential homes.

The authorities have since switched to non-recyclable composite material with zero scrap value. Now, thieves target public utility and industrial cables, made valuable by surging copper and metal prices.
Top targets: telecom and rail copper cables, reflected by the recent Express Rail Link (ERL) airport corridor and national Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cable thefts.
Thieves brazenly infiltrate substations and restricted rail lines to steal copper busbars and drain transformer oil that are illegally processed and resold as industrial lubricant.
Once petty thieves, they have morphed into organised syndicates, systematically siphoning public property and reselling them by the kilo.

Fenceable items must possess intrinsic value, no traceable serial numbers and an eager black market: easy to hide or transport, cut, unbolt or carry, and available in unsecured or predictable locations that yield high cash-per-kilo or cash-per-unit.
High demand is a given, but this is critical: stolen items are linked to a nefarious network of buyers — operators of unregulated scrap yards, rogue pawnshops or online buyers.
The recent cable thefts at the ERL track network and the Salak Tinggi station may net thieves between RM6,500 and RM13,000 —a day's work capitalising on high global copper prices.
To stop the thieves, authorities must stymie the rogues' ability to operate and their supply chain. Once indicted, penalties must include imprisonment and heavy fines.
In the long term, the best deterrent is to choke their market by inspecting and revoking licences of unscrupulous scrap disposal factories and illegal scrap metal dealers.
These dealers must digitally log all copper sales, to be cross-referenced against public utility logs for missing cables. Also go after every conceivable fence.
Prasarana and Malaysia Rail Link have shifted to intelligent CCTV using artificial intelligence to trigger alerts, marking cables with invisible trace-element liquid and embedding micro-trackers.

Repeated thefts of critical infrastructure seriously threaten public safety, essential services and economic activity. Define the thefts as a national security threat marshalled by relevant pre-emptive laws.
The priority is implementation, backed by clear responsibilities, coordinated intelligence-sharing and measurable enforcement results.
a2012d10c433449f: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of jobs created from data centre investments is not directly proportional to the value of investments announced, says human resources minister R Ramanan.

In a written parliamentary reply, Ramanan said this was because data centres are capital-intensive projects, with much of the investment going toward high-quality equipment, electrical infrastructure and cooling systems.
“The majority of jobs created in this sector are high-value and require specialised technical skills,” he said.

Ramanan was responding to Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail (PH-Bandar Tun Razak), who asked for the latest statistics on the number of high-skilled jobs created for Malaysians through data centre investments.
Data centre and cloud computing projects attracted RM95.8 billion in investments in the first half of this year, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida).

Malaysia recorded RM385.7 billion in data centre-related investments from 2021 to the first half of 2026, reflecting strong investor confidence among global technology companies such as Microsoft, Google and Amazon.
Ramanan said the ministry, through Talent Corporation Malaysia Bhd (TalentCorp), had identified 12 high-demand job roles in the data centre sector, most of which require specialised technical skills.

They include electrical and mechanical engineers, IT project managers, commissioning engineers, solutions architects, network security engineers, facility managers, data centre technicians, facility technicians and chargemen.

Of the 12 roles, eight require a degree, one requires a diploma and two require technical and vocational education and training (TVET) qualifications. Chargemen must have an SPM qualification and at least a B4 certificate of competency from the Energy Commission.
Ramanan said this showed that the sector offers employment opportunities to both university graduates and graduates of local TVET institutions.
Malaysia has 125 data centres with 925.6MW of live capacity, 2GW under construction and another 3.1GW planned, according to a report by research firm BMI.
Despite growing competition from Vietnam and Thailand, BMI expects Malaysia to remain Southeast Asia's leading data centre market.
However, there have been widely reported concerns that the surge in data centre investments in Malaysia could strain water and electricity supplies.

3e63e5cce7d2ad16: It's the end of support for Office 2021 LTSC and it seems like Microsoft is celebrating with a Microsoft 365 outage for some European customers. The affected service is Global Secure Access (GSA), which customers use to access services including Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Teams, and Windows 365 Cloud PCs. We'd argue the "365" moniker is perhaps a little inaccurate at this point. According to Microsoft, the cause is: "A section of GSA infrastructure is performing below acceptable performance thresholds, affecting connectivity to Microsoft 365 services and resulting in impact." The company is applying traffic and performance optimizations, and the system is now showing signs of life, which is scant comfort for customers who have struggled to access Microsoft 365 services using GSA. The timing is unfortunate, since it coincides with the end of support for Office LTSC 2021, Microsoft's on-premises version of Office. The company would like customers to migrate to Microsoft 365, though on-premises Office LTSC 2024 is also available if the cloud doesn't tickle their fancy. It's not yet clear what caused the latest outage. Microsoft is having to report status updates on its Service Health Status page because, according to the company, "Microsoft 365 administrators may be unable to access the admin center to get Service health information." We checked, and, above the cheery text, "Great! No active issues," is a message that reads: "We are having trouble getting info about your service incidents, advisories, and history right now. Try again in a few minutes." Enterprises have already decided whether to stick with on-premises Office, move to the cloud, or choose something else altogether. While Office 2021 LTSC won't suddenly stop working, the end of support from Microsoft will require customers to take some action for compliance reasons, if nothing else. Those who have taken the leap to Microsoft 365 will be pondering the wisdom of their move as Microsoft has demonstrated, yet again, that its cloud services are not quite as reliable as customers might hope or need, and an "oops, sorry about that" only goes so far where a loss of productivity is concerned. ®
d527cf335c881306: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has settled RM17.15 billion in excess tax refunds involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases as at Sept 30, 2026.

d26d6dd7329bf100: KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani Submarine Cable Connection (Salam) is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and be completed by the fourth quarter of 2029, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had issued an invitation for the project and was evaluating it. The implementing party is expected to be appointed by the fourth quarter of 2026.
The project aims to strengthen communications connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

"It involves developing a high-capacity domestic submarine cable system with diverse network routes and backup capabilities to strengthen the resilience of the country's communications infrastructure," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Meanwhile, Phase Two of the Jendela (National Digital Network) project is expected to begin in November, covering 1,000 sites nationwide, including 352 in Sabah.
Fahmi said internet coverage at the sites would be expanded through 4G cellular services, a combination of 4G and 5G, or satellite broadband, depending on local conditions and needs.
Kinabatangan accounts for the largest share of the 352 sites in Sabah, with 106, followed by Pensiangan with 55, Kota Marudu with 36, Kalabakan with 29 and Kudat with 26.

The remaining sites are in Tuaran (23), Penampang and Ranau (15 each), Sipitang (13), Kimanis (12), Sepanggar (six), Papar (five), Batu Sapi (four), Beaufort and Tawau (three each), and Putatan (one).
"The government, through MCMC, would continue to assess needs in other areas of Sabah, including Putatan, for possible expansion, subject to priorities and funding availability," he said.

The RM5 billion Jendela project aims to improve internet connectivity and bridge the digital divide, including in rural and remote areas and Orang Asli villages. It also targets connectivity along 7,000km of roads and highways and 1,700km of rail routes nationwide.
Fahmi was responding to a question from Datuk Shahelmey Yahya (BN-Putatan) on the status of Salam in Sabah and areas identified for Jendela Phase Two.
868ae14b5a08f1ca: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's administration has asked his ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign, the White House said Tuesday, amid allegations that she sought money from a Trump supporter and accepted lavish hospitality from wealthy Greek businessmen.
"We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," Trump's new press secretary Katie Zacharia told reporters at her first White House briefing.
The announcement came a day after Trump acknowledged that he was considering dismissing Guilfoyle, a former Fox News host and ex-fiancee of his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr.
"Well, we're looking at it. Yeah, we're not happy," Trump told reporters Monday when asked about her future.
Guilfoyle has faced mounting scrutiny following a series of reports by The Wall Street Journal about her financial dealings and relationships with wealthy businessmen.
The newspaper reported that she asked Eric Deters, an influential Trump supporter, to pay off US$100,000 in personal credit card debt shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025.

"Honey, please, I need you to get this done for me today," she wrote to Deters in a message accompanied by instructions for paying her credit card company, according to the Journal, which published screenshots of the exchanges.
Deters refused to make the payment, telling the newspaper that doing so would have cost him his marriage.
Guilfoyle's lawyer has disputed the authenticity of the messages and denied wrongdoing.

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle boasted of luxury trips and hotel stays funded by wealthy Greek businessmen, citing hundreds of messages, emails and other records, including recorded conversations.
She travelled to the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, aboard a private jet with Alexandros Exarchou, chief executive of Greek construction company Aktor Group, according to the newspaper.

Guilfoyle also spent Christmas at the exclusive Swiss ski resort of Gstaad with Greek shipping magnate Nikolas Tsakos and stayed at a luxury Paris hotel on a trip with him, with Tsakos footing the bill, the Journal reported.
The state department's inspector general is investigating whether Guilfoyle received improper gifts, according to US media reports.
The revelations emerged as secretary of state Marco Rubio visited Europe last week, including a stop in Athens, where he declined to comment on the allegations.
Guilfoyle, a prominent figure in Trump's Make America Great Again movement, was appointed ambassador after her engagement to Donald Trump Jr ended.
A former prosecutor and television commentator, she was previously married to California's Democratic governor Gavin Newsom.
It was not immediately clear whether Guilfoyle had agreed to step down following the White House request.
5aa486f383de0553: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Ahli Parlimen PAS cadang kerajaan perkenal silabus kemandirian dan daya tahan di peringkat sekolah, institusi pengajian tinggi, dan komuniti bagi membolehkan rakyat membuat persiapan lebih baik berdepan bencana serta kecemasan.

Mumtaz Nawi (PN-Tumpat), berkata kemahiran praktikal ikhtiar hidup patut diserapkan ke dalam silabus pendidikan, terutamanya ketika negara bersiap sedia menghadapi kemungkinan fenomena Super El Niño tahun hadapan.
Berucap di Dewan Rakyat, beliau memberi amaran Malaysia berdepan risiko cuaca panas ekstrem antara Februari dan Mei 2027, dengan suhu berpotensi melebihi 41°C.
Beliau berkata, silabus yang dicadangkan itu sepatutnya membekalkan rakyat Malaysia dengan kemahiran praktikal mengendalikan situasi kecemasan, bukannya kepada pengetahuan teori semata-mata.

"Ia perlu merangkumi kesiapsiagaan bencana merentasi isu banjir, termasuk cuaca panas ekstrem, pertolongan cemas, pengurusan kewangan ketika krisis, kecemasan keselamatan siber, serta gangguan bekalan air, makanan, dan tenaga,” katanya.
Mumtaz turut merujuk Jepun dan Filipina sebagai contoh negara yang mengambil langkah memperkukuh kesiapsiagaan dan ketahanan bencana.

Beliau menyeru rangka kerja kesiapsiagaan iklim yang komprehensif diwujudkan, termasuk peta dan kalendar iklim bagi meningkatkan keupayaan negara menangani risiko yang semakin meningkat susulan perubahan iklim.

Sebelum ini, Jabatan Meteorologi meramalkan cuaca panas terik antara Mac dan Mei tahun hadapan disebabkan fenomena Super El Niño, yang mampu menyaksikan suhu melepasi rekod tertinggi Malaysia, 40.1°C.
Ketua Pengarah Hisham Anip, berkata analisis terhadap fenomena El Niño semasa, berasimilasi dengan kesan perubahan iklim dan pemanasan global menunjukkan suhu berisiko melebihi 41°C.

27840f9e16516c3f: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has seized 2,380 squishy toys worth RM30,391 over suspected non-compliance with safety standards since Oct 3.
Its director, Mohd Mufsi Lat, said the soft, sponge-like toys, which came in various shapes and designs, were seized following 101 inspections across the state.
He said the inspections found that the toys allegedly did not carry the Malaysian conformity (MC) mark, as required under the relevant regulations.
"Action was taken against six premises in Kuala Terengganu, with investigations opened under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 and regulations governing toy safety standards.

f5c7debf62c4b248: PETALING JAYA: Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain yang berlangsung di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) awal bulan ini menjana impak ekonomi hampir RM950 juta, menurut Kementerian Belia dan Sukan (KBS).

Memetik angka daripada Formula 1 Management, Menteri Belia dan Sukan Dr Taufiq Johari, berkata acara pada 2 hingga 4 Okt itu menarik kira-kira 261,000 peminat, termasuk dianggarkan 103,000 penonton pada hari perlumbaan, selain ditonton 827 juta penonton di seluruh dunia.

Beliau berkata SIC sedang melaksanakan penilaian itu bersama firma perunding yang dilantik bagi meneliti kos penganjuran dan impak ekonomi perlumbaan berkenaan.

22988a7b585ab423: PETALING JAYA: A PAS MP has called for survival and resilience education to be introduced in schools, higher education institutions and communities to better prepare Malaysians for disasters and emergencies.
Mumtaz Nawi (PN-Tumpat) said practical survival skills should be incorporated into the education syllabus, particularly as Malaysia braces for a possible Super El Niño phenomenon next year.
Speaking in the Dewan Rakyat today, she warned that Malaysia could experience extreme heat between February and May 2027, with temperatures potentially exceeding 41°C.
She said the proposed syllabus should equip Malaysians with practical skills to handle emergencies rather than focus solely on theoretical knowledge.

“It should cover disaster preparedness beyond floods, including extreme heat, first aid, financial management during crises, cybersecurity emergencies, and disruptions to water, food and energy supplies,” she said.
Mumtaz also cited Japan and the Philippines as examples of countries that had taken steps to strengthen disaster preparedness and resilience.
She called for a comprehensive climate preparedness framework, including a climate map and calendar, to improve Malaysia's ability to respond to the growing risks posed by climate change.

The meteorological department has forecast scorching weather between March and May next year due to the Super El Niño phenomenon, which could see temperatures surpass Malaysia's record high of 40.1°C.
Its director-general, Hisham Anip, said an analysis of the current El Niño phenomenon, combined with the effects of climate change and global warming, suggested that temperatures could exceed 41°C.
He said the department was also working with the health ministry to develop a heat index to establish thresholds for warning the public about health risks associated with hot weather.
6722327b9652272f: SHANGHAI: Top-seeded Alexander Zverev toughed out two tie-breaks to beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (8/6), 4-6, 7-6 (7/1) at the Shanghai Masters on Tuesday, winning his first match since being guaranteed the year-end world number one ranking.
The 29-year-old German will play Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals.
"Really difficult match," Zverev said.
"I had some physical issues, so, you know, I was maybe slower," he told the crowd.
"My ankle was acting up, unfortunately, again," Zverev elaborated in an on-court interview, without giving specifics.
"I'm starting to feel my body more, but I'm happy to be through."
Zverev, the current world number two, was guaranteed the year-end number one spot after third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz lost to Zizou Bergs in Shanghai on Monday.
On Tuesday, Zverev called the honour "special", saying it was a different feeling to winning tournaments, adding he was "looking forward" to the responsibility of owning that status.
Neither player could create much trouble for his opponent in the first set as they traded aces to hold serve.
But Zverev found himself under pressure when he was forced to save a set point before making it into a tie-breaker.
He kept his composure as Bublik squandered three set points in a row, taking the first set with a commanding forehand at the net.

That momentum was cut short when Bublik broke the German's serve in the fifth game of the second set. Despite a few clutch backhands, a sombre-looking Zverev was unable to avoid tumbling into a deciding third.
The players soon found themselves staring down another tie-break, but this time Zverev raced to a 6-1 lead and closed out the match with an ace.
Gea goes on
Earlier, 56th-ranked Arthur Gea put on a convincing show to beat Jakub Mensik 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 in their fourth-round encounter.

Mensik, ranked 15th, hit the ground trying to convert a crucial break point in the final minutes of the second set, but Gea got past his opponent with a cross-court backhand and won on his first match point.
"I'm enjoying how I'm playing. I feel I'm improving all the time," said Gea, the lowest-ranked player left in the draw.
Asked if he might recreate last year's "miracle" that saw Valentin Vacherot claim the title as world number 204, Gea said he would "see what happens".
"I don't think it's a miracle when you work hard every day, but I hope to do the same," he said.
Two days earlier the 21-year-old Frenchman beat US Open finalist Ben Shelton, the third seed, 7-6 (7/5), 7-6 (7/3) in the third round for the biggest victory of his career.
bff7165dbcc3c76a: DOHA: Qatar's revenues fell 42% in the first half of 2026, its emir said on Tuesday, as gas infrastructure and exports took a severe hit during the Middle East war.

Qatar, the world's second-largest exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG) after the US, lost a "significant proportion" of its exports, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani told in the annual session of the Shura Council advisory body in Doha.

"The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, together with the direct damage inflicted on some energy facilities in Ras Laffan Industrial City, disrupted a significant portion of the country's exports," the emir said.
"It is only natural that the crisis would have a negative impact on public finances, as the total revenues declined by 42% during the first half of the year," he added.
Iranian strikes badly damaged the Ras Laffan site, and Qatar's exports have been hobbled by Iran's blockade of Hormuz – the only route for its LNG shipments.
However, a major expansion of North Field, the world's biggest gas field, is going ahead, the emir said.
"Work on the expansion of the North Field Gas project is progressing according to the set plans," he told the council.
The expansion at North Field, which stretches under the Gulf to Iranian territory, aims to increase Qatar's total production capacity to 142 million tonnes per year by 2030.
The Golden Pass LNG project, being carried out in the United States in partnership with ExxonMobil, has also "made significant progress", he said.
Qatar is one of the Gulf countries hit hardest by the war. On Tuesday, the International Monetary Fund forecast a 15.6% drop in its GDP this year in its latest global report.
23f8591ddbcecc53: OCTOBER 13 — Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are a group of 17 metallic elements which are found beneath the Earth’s surface in the Earth’s crust.
Accordingly, RREs constitute “land”. By definition, the word includes, among others, “the earth below the surface and all substances therein”. (See Section 3 of the National Land Code)
Land, in turn, is a state matter. (See Item 2 of the State List of the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution).

More than a year ago in August, then Acting Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani had explained that his ministry had no plans to establish a centralised body to regulate Malaysia’s REE industry.
Johari cited constitutional provisions — that is, the State List in the Ninth Schedule — as giving states authority over mining permits, leases and licences.

The minister also alluded to objections from state governments, saying several states had raised concerns during engagement sessions, viewing the proposal as an attempt to nationalise state-owned mineral resources.
Any move to centralise REE regulation therefore would require in-depth study and close consultation with all state governments to safeguard their rights.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

File picture for illustrative purposes only. The author says the proposed national entity for rare earth elements must not be seen as an attempt to nationalise state-owned mineral resources, as land matters fall under state jurisdiction. — Unsplash pic
Johari said so when winding up the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) debate for his ministry.

Petroleum resources are different. The Federal List in the Ninth Schedule includes Item 8 on “Trade, commerce and industry” which in turn includes “Development of mineral resources; mines, mining, minerals and mineral ores; oils and oilfields; purchase, sale, import and export of minerals and mineral ores; petroleum products; regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields” subject to Item 2(c) in the State List.
So, it is curious that Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin should propose the establishment of a national entity to manage REE as a new source of national wealth in the post-petroleum era.

Hamzah said the entity — to be known as Reenas — was necessary to prevent non-radioactive raw materials worth more than RM800 billion from being sold cheaply without value-added processing or lost through illegal mining activities.
The intentions are good.
Five months ago, Professor Datuk Dr Ahmad Ibrahim wrote on REE as follows:

“Now, we face a new frontier: rare earths. The world is clamoring for them. They are the invisible heartbeat of electric vehicles, smartphones, and advanced defense systems. And here we sit, on potentially significant deposits. It is a second chance at industrial glory. But immediately, the scaremongers emerge. We hear the same words—radiation, thorium, danger—but this time they are amplified by a global network of non-governmental organizations and a sensationalist media. We must ask ourselves a hard question: Why?”
The reason may be in the famous saying: the road to hell is paved with good intentions.
It means that merely intending to do something good is not enough, and well-meaning actions can often lead to disastrous or harmful results.
Perhaps Johari was right: in-depth study and close consultation with all state governments to safeguard their rights are required.
That’s what federalism is all about.
If a centralised body to regulate Malaysia’s REE industry must not be seen as an attempt to nationalise state-owned mineral resources, what more a Petronas-like national entity on REE.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
ec003ec20ed7c3a4: NetBSD seems to be thriving of late: as the Linux world goes pro-AI, some of the AI-averse are turning to this explicitly AI-free project. The NetBSD project’s Mastodon feed reports that it received a record 120 donations last month, and it has far exceeded its target: “We received $120,282 USD in total. Naturally, this has completely filled up our donations target bar which was set at $50,000. Time to fund some projects!” It’s a welcome contrast to the usual stories of under-funded FOSS projects, and it follows a visible uptick in people asking about NetBSD in the FOSS Unix groups we read, ever since Emperor Penguin Torvalds said that Linux was not an anti-AI project back in July, and the following month, the Debian project polled its developers on AI use, and they chose to permit AI-generated contributions. This is the moderate, centrist stance. The most recent Ubuntu Summit was heavily AI-flavored. The heads of Red Hat Global Engineering sent out a memo about transitioning to an Agentic Software Development Lifecycle. But once it’s in the kernel, then no distro can totally avoid it. This stance is profoundly offputting to those who prefer hand-crafted code. Last week, the Reg FOSS desk attended the Open Source Summit Europe in Prague. This event reflects the tendencies of the increasingly mainstream open-source world: Linux is pretty much the only OS in evidence, although many attendees tote around (and present from) MacBooks, and both Microsoft and Windows were visible. The event overlaps with Embedded Linux Conference, so the Zephyr RTOS was also visible on some robots and other gadgets. The Open Source Summit gives the overall impression that Linux is the only general-purpose FOSS OS. We saw no mention at all of any of the BSDs; indeed, when we mentioned NetBSD, some of the folks from Let’s Encrypt looked puzzled and asked us “What’s ‘net bee ess dee’?” Sadly, this is probably a reasonably fair representation of its presence at the event and in the FOSS mainstream. For us, the single most dominant theme in the talks, the materials, the stands, and even the T-shirts was AI. It’s everywhere, and every exhibitor was keen to talk about how they’re using AI, deploying AI, scaling AI, or managing AI. The louder the noise about AI gets, the stronger grows the aversion of those of us who actively wish to avoid it. The NetBSD project, on the other hand, came out early and strongly: it banned AI-generated code back in 2024, just a month after the project celebrated its 30th anniversary. This vulture attended the project’s talk at that year’s FOSDEM: NetBSD 10: Thirty years, still going strong!. As ever, the question of differentiation between the BSDs, and between Linux and the BSDs, came up. NetBSD’s slogan is “Of course it runs NetBSD,” but in 2024, its ubiquity was looking threatened: Linux is comparable, and FreeBSD boast close integration with ZFS, Linux-compatible Podman containers, and more. The following year, though, FreeBSD 15 appeared, dropping support for 32-bit x86 (and 32-bit POWER). Debian 13 dropped x86-32 too, as well as MIPS CPU support. That year, the RHEL 10 release went further: it not only requires 64-bit x86, it demands x86-64-v3. This cut off so many older machines, it forced CERN to start switching to Debian. From within the BSD world, the differences between the various projects are fairly clear. NetBSD is minimal, highly portable, and takes great pride in its very friendly, welcoming community. We can personally attest to this: in the course of our review of NetBSD 11, we tried to install the veteran CDE desktop. We couldn’t get it working, but the folks on the NetBSD mailing list tried very hard indeed to help. Although it also has very broad platform support, OpenBSD’s focus is on security, to the extent of dropping the entire Bluetooth subsystem because it didn’t measure up. Its community is far less tolerant: indeed, when this vulture’s latest OpenBSD review was posted on the OpenBSD sub-Reddit, we were banned from the group for pointing out errors in their negative assessments of a very positive article. OpenBSD project lead Theo de Raadt has said it cannot accept AI-generated code: any submitter lacks the right to place a license on it, because it’s impossible to trace which humans originally wrote any code that LLMs regurgitate. However, this guideline seems permeable: the tmux app, the terminal multiplexer included in OpenBSD, has already accepted AI-assisted changes. We asked de Raadt for official comment on this and he declined. FreeBSD is the 362.87 kg gorilla of the BSDs, to the extent that the mainline OS has its own distros, such as GhostBSD, plus MidnightBSD. There’s also the recently-revived experimental NextBSD, and a couple of NAS distros. There’s a live OS called NomadBSD too, although we had little success with this. However, FreeBSD’s central committee has been debating whether to permit AI-generated code for over a year now: we first reported on it in September 2025, and there’s still no consensus. We are sure there is a large helping of “AI is just a tool”, and we suspect side-dishes of “AI is here to stay” and “don’t get left behind.” If anyone dares point out failings, doubtless they’re using the wrong model, or not prompting it correctly. NetBSD’s position is clear: “Do not commit tainted code to the repository. “Code generated by a large language model or similar technology, such as GitHub/Microsoft’s Copilot, OpenAI’s ChatGPT, or Facebook/Meta’s Code Llama, is presumed to be tainted code, and must not be committed without prior written approval by core.” So far, this seems to be serving it well. If as a result, it remains relatively tiny and minimal, and gets left behind by the AI wave, we plan to be right there with it. Long may the project continue. Bootnote We won’t wish to omit anyone. There is another BSD: Dragonfly BSD, which is experimenting with the kernel and filesystem design. We gave version 6.4 a spin in 2023 and since then there have been only two minor point releases: version 6.4.2 was nearly a year and a half ago, although development is still active. We are not aware that the project has made any statement for or against LLM code generation. Perhaps it should. ®
9db61c66a8c2042b: PETALING JAYA: The F1 Bahrain Grand Prix held at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) earlier this month generated an economic impact of nearly RM950 million, says the youth and sports ministry.

Citing figures from Formula 1 Management, youth and sports minister Dr Taufiq Johari said the Oct 2-4 event attracted about 261,000 fans, including an estimated 103,000 on race day, and was watched by 827 million viewers worldwide.
He also said that more than 97,000 tickets were sold, while over 50,000 international tourists and about 5,000 foreign workers came to Malaysia for the event.

“The presence of overseas spectators also increased revenue for the tourism, hospitality and aviation sectors, as well as local small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and strengthened Malaysia’s profile as a world-class sports and investment destination,” he said in a written parliamentary reply to Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong).
Rodiyah had asked the youth and sports ministry for the estimated economic benefit compared with the costs borne by the government, and whether a cost-benefit assessment would be carried out.
However, Taufiq said the government had yet to determine whether hosting the event was worthwhile, as a cost-benefit assessment was still under way.
He said SIC was conducting the assessment with an appointed consulting firm to examine the hosting costs and economic impact of the race.

"The findings of the cost-benefit assessment will serve as one of the considerations for the government in determining whether it is appropriate for Malaysia to consider hosting F1 again in future," he said.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Bahrain GP following an agreement between Formula 1, the FIA, and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement kept the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
SIC hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017 before it was removed from the calendar because of rising hosting costs and licensing fees.
7f9bf26e405227e6: KOTA KINABALU: Schools in Sabah will be temporarily closed if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 150 for three consecutive days, the state government has announced.
State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the measure was taken to protect pupils and teachers from the adverse health effects of haze.
"This measure is also in line with the Education Ministry's directive following the advice of Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim," he said in a statement today.
As of 7pm, Tawau was the only district to record an API reading above the threshold, at 155.
All schools in Tawau have been ordered to close from tomorrow amid worsening haze conditions.
9119e8d6a489fe8b: BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed deep disappointment over the international order's failure to address the Palestinian cause, describing it as a failure to uphold democracy and human rights.
Anwar questioned the consistency of the international community in upholding these principles, saying Palestinians should not be subjected to different standards of treatment.
"What is so hypocritical is the failure of the international community. I have to speak as the prime minister, and I understand that.

"But I have to express my utter disgust with the failure of the international order. What order is there without democracy and human rights, when human beings are treated like animals and slaves?" he said in his speech at the Sumud Nusantara Dinner today.
The dinner was held in conjunction with the Global Sumud Congress 2026.

Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Sumud Nusantara Command Centre director-general Datuk Dr Ahmad Sani Araby.
Anwar said generations in formerly colonised countries had fought colonialism and imperialism because they opposed injustice, oppression and colonisation.
"Now, we are in a society that condones the very same principles we fought against for decades under colonialism and imperialism," he said.
Citing Gaza, Anwar said the suffering of Palestinians should not be viewed as a recent development, but understood in the context of decades of oppression.
"Some say it has only happened in the past few years, but those who understand history know that this oppression has continued for 70 years.
"What is the problem? Is it because they are the Arabs, Palestinians and Muslims? There is no answer.
"Why is it that, when it comes to the Palestinian cause, there is a different set of arrangements, judgments and decisions?" he said.

Anwar added that he had raised the issue with counterparts in Europe, the United States and elsewhere, questioning whether Palestinians were being treated differently because of their religious or ethnic identities.
"To me, it does not matter. What is important is that they are human beings, and they cannot be colonised," he said.
025fe35143c06903: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Association of Film Exhibitors (MAFE) has welcomed the Prime Minister's 2027 Budget announcement that local film screenings and theatre performances in the Federal Territories will be exempt from entertainment duty, starting Jan 1, 2027.
In a statement released today, MAFE said that it views the move as a positive step towards supporting Malaysia's creative industries and strengthening the local film ecosystem.
Following the Prime Minister's call for similar exemptions across all states, MAFE also plans to engage with state governments to encourage nationwide adoption.
The association looks forward to working alongside the Ministry of Communications and the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) to ensure smooth implementation.
MAFE and its members remain committed to championing local content and supporting the continued growth of Malaysia's film industry.
The 2027 Budget will also provide a major boost to Malaysia's creative arts sector via a RM130 million allocation to strengthen local film, music, and digital content.
The funding includes special financial incentives for both local and international filmmakers who choose to shoot in Malaysia.
Extra perks will go to projects that showcase and celebrate the country's culture and identity.
Local animators will also receive dedicated aid to create 20 new original character brands to bring uniquely Malaysian stories to the global stage.

753a5438c6d16b8a: OCTOBER 13 — The passage of the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2024 marks a historic milestone in ending decades of citizenship inequality for Malaysian women. Overwhelmingly passed by both houses of Parliament by December 2024, it received Royal Assent on March 7, 2025 and was officially gazetted on March 20, 2025. But as of today, the amendments remain inoperative, and the official implementation date is yet to be announced.

Meanwhile, this landmark legislative reform remains incomplete and hollow. Without its enforcement, Malaysian women continue to be denied equal citizenship rights, and are forced to bear the harm caused by this ongoing discrimination.

This harmful effect is particularly pronounced for pregnant Malaysian women living overseas. As long as the reform is not in effect, their children who are born abroad are not able to acquire Malaysian citizenship by operation of law.

“Melissa” (pseudonym used to protect identity), who is due to give birth in a few months, must choose between undertaking a high-risk, and financially burdensome journey in her third trimester to give birth in Malaysia, or deliver her baby abroad and depend on a long and cumbersome citizenship application process under Article 15(2). She is residing in a third country, and her non-Malaysian husband is also unable to pass on his citizenship to their child. Without access to a nationality, the child cannot obtain the necessary visas to remain in a foreign country, leaving the family in a deeply precarious situation. Although Parliament has passed reforms meant to address this, the relief the Amendment would provide remains out of reach.

According to the authors, this landmark legislative reform remains incomplete and hollow. Without its enforcement, Malaysian women continue to be denied equal citizenship rights, and are forced to bear the harm caused by this ongoing discrimination. — Pexels.com pic

For recently married Malaysian women like Tiana, who reside overseas with their non-Malaysian spouses, the delay in enforcement has created uncertainty about their ability to plan their future families. For Tiana, seeing her brother able to pass on Malaysian citizenship to his child born abroad without facing the same administrative barriers, highlights the unequal position Malaysian women continue to face. She is concerned that in the absence of clear and timely implementation, she may one day have to consider returning to Malaysia to give birth, potentially putting her own health and that of her unborn child at risk during the journey, in order to secure citizenship for her child. Tiana stresses that no Malaysian mother should be forced to choose between giving birth safely where they live and ensuring their child receives the Malaysian citizenship that is rightfully theirs.

Civil society organisations acknowledge the significant progress made by the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail in processing pending citizenship applications, which has brought relief to many Malaysian families.

However, with every passing day, another child is born to suffer the discriminatory effects of this unenforced law. To ensure that Malaysian women and their children no longer face similar uncertainties and delays, the passage of the amendment must now be accompanied by the timely implementation of the Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025.

Parliament has fulfilled its legislative duty. It is now incumbent upon the Executive to enforce the law. It is the final, essential step to ensure that no newborn Anak Malaysia is left stateless or stranded in limbo by administrative delay.
