c8069e3520a39950: BATU PAHAT: A trailer driver was killed after his vehicle rear-ended a lorry on the North-South Expressway near Ayer Hitam.
Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Abd Rahim Razali said the 56-year-old man was confirmed dead at the scene by a medical team.
The accident occurred at 3.50pm at KM93.5 of the northbound North-South Expressway. The trailer was carrying wooden pallets, while the lorry was transporting a skylift.
Abd Rahim said the trailer hit the rear of the lorry, causing the wooden pallets to crush the trailer's cab and trapping the driver.
The lorry driver and his assistant, both in their 40s, survived.
d1371e2e191f9068: PETALING JAYA: Ahli Parlimen Kepong, Lim Lip Eng mempersoalkan kelewatan pelaksanaan penggunaan kamera badan polis di seluruh negara, sambil berkata kerajaan sebelum ini menyasarkan pelaksanaannya sepenuhnya menjelang suku pertama 2025.

Ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat, Lim berkata Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail pernah memaklumkan kepadanya melalui jawapan Parlimen pada Oktober 2023 bahawa polis dijangka dilengkapi sepenuhnya dengan kamera badan menjelang awal 2025.
“Kini kita sudah memasuki suku keempat 2026. Apa yang berlaku kepada janji itu?” soalnya.

Lim turut mendakwa menerima aduan bahawa sesetengah anggota polis melakukan pemeriksaan telefon bimbit tanpa alasan munasabah dan memeras wang daripada orang awam, termasuk warga asing yang tidak membawa pasport.
Beliau menggesa polis mendedahkan jumlah aduan yang diterima berhubung salah laku sedemikian, serta bilangan anggota yang disiasat, didakwa atau dibuang kerja.

Beliau turut bertanya sama ada terdapat anggota polis yang enggan memakai kamera badan atau sengaja mematikannya ketika bertugas. Jika ada, katanya, tindakan tatatertib perlu dikenakan terhadap mereka.

Lim menggesa kerajaan menetapkan garis masa yang jelas bagi pelaksanaan penuh penggunaan kamera badan serta mewujudkan prosedur khusus untuk penyimpanan rakaman, kawalan akses kepada rakaman dan hukuman terhadap anggota yang mengusik bukti.

“Anggota polis yang jujur tidak sepatutnya takut kepada kamera badan. Orang awam diminta menghormati polis, tetapi polis juga mesti membuktikan bahawa mereka layak menerima penghormatan itu,” katanya.
Tahun lalu, lebih 7,000 kamera badan telah diagihkan ke 157 ibu pejabat polis daerah dan 640 balai polis.
66dac4c8c1c40472: KUALA LUMPUR: An Armed Forces personnel was killed after falling about 5m from a flyover onto another motorcyclist on the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) near Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) this morning.

Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief assistant commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at 8.04am as the 24-year-old soldier was travelling from his home in Bukit Jalil to his workplace at Sungai Besi Camp.
He said the soldier, who was riding a Honda Wave motorcycle, was believed to have lost control while negotiating a ramp on the flyover near TBS to make a U-turn.
The soldier was thrown onto the road below, while his motorcycle remained on the flyover.
"The victim landed on a 46-year-old man riding a Honda Vario motorcycle from Cheras towards Sungai Besi, causing both to fall onto the road.
"At the same time, a lorry driven by a 46-year-old man tried to avoid the two victims but failed and hit the Honda Vario motorcycle," he said in a statement today.
Zamzuri said the soldier sustained severe head and bodily injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
The Honda Vario rider suffered a fractured left arm, facial injuries and internal head bleeding. He was taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz for treatment.
Mohd Zamzuri said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged members of the public or witnesses with information to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station to assist in the investigation.
e5da90770d10058b: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia aims to attract about 250,000 international students by 2030, focusing on a diversity of source countries to strengthen its position as a preferred higher education destination.
Higher education minister Zambry Abdul Kadir said about 170,000 international students from 180 countries are currently pursuing their studies in Malaysia.

"When there are many students from various countries, Malaysia becomes a good destination for them to study," he told reporters after closing the 2026 International Young Future Leaders (iFUTURE) Summit at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here.
Zambry said the presence of international students is projected to contribute at least RM16 billion a year to the national economy.
He added that the projection does not account for the spillover effects of other economic activities that also generate income for local businesses.
When asked about monitoring graduates, Zambry said the higher education ministry uses the MyMOHES system to track their employment progress over a three-year period.
He said the system enables the ministry to regularly review the status and progress of graduates.
6bad21365a971d0a: Microsoft has lifted the lid on the next generation of its Azure Maia custom AI chips, saying it will usher in a new phase of its compute infrastructure where everything is closely integrated to meet the demands of agentic inference. The Redmond giant says its Azure Maia 200, announced earlier this year, is now serving production workloads and that a successor is already planned for 2027. Azure Maia 300 is described as "a complete intelligent system" designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today. Microsoft claims a full 96-accelerator configuration will deliver up to seven times Maia 200's rack-scale token throughput, while offering 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Its next-gen chip is created with an inference-first architecture optimized for long-context, memory-intensive and decode-heavy AI workloads, according to a blog post by Microsoft's EVP for Cloud and AI, Scott Guthrie. The firm envisions it being deployed in rack-scale systems comprising up to 96 accelerators, while each Maia 300 will feature eight HBM4 memory stacks providing up to 18 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth, the better to support execution of large models and long-context workloads. This sounds similar to the kind of rack-scale AI equipment that has already been developed by Nvidia for its GPU accelerators, and more recently by AMD with its Helion and Helios infrastructure, all designed to make the most of their own specific silicon and software stacks. Microsoft says that Maia 300 is "built as a complete system, with software, silicon, physical rack infrastructure, networking, and datacenters co-designed to operate as a single platform to meet the demands of cloud-scale agentic inference." It insists that this system-level approach is necessary for agentic workloads, which involve multi-step execution, long-context decoding and tool use, and "change the computational profile and arithmetic intensity of inference." The growing emphasis on in-house integration contrasts with Microsoft's 2024 "AI Access Principles," which stressed partnerships across its technology stack. The firm even complained to the European Commission's competition authorities that Google had a competitive advantage because of its approach. "Only one company – Google," said Microsoft at the time, "is vertically integrated in a manner that provides it with strength and independence at every AI layer from chips to a thriving mobile app store. Everybody else must rely on partnerships to innovate and compete." Microsoft now has its own AI chips, rack-scale designs, and internally developed MAI models, giving it more control over its stack. It plans to scale Azure Maia to "multi-gigawatt deployments" starting in 2027. We asked Microsoft for comment. Guthrie said that the firm will share more details on its strategy at next month's Microsoft Ignite 2026 event in San Francisco. ®
9ae85d72037c16b2: PETALING JAYA: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) sedang menyiasat kejadian seorang lelaki tular memandu kereta sehingga memasuki kawasan landasan Stesen KTMB Jalan Limbungan di Pelabuhan Klang, pada 11 Okt.

fe7227c477206e95: PETALING JAYA: Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng has questioned the delay in the nationwide rollout of police body cameras, saying the government had targeted full implementation by the first quarter of 2025.

Debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat, Lim said home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had told him in a parliamentary reply in October 2023 that police were expected to be fully equipped with body cameras by early 2025.
"We are now in the fourth quarter of 2026. What happened to that promise?" he asked.

Lim also alleged that he had received complaints of some police officers conducting unwarranted searches of mobile phones and extorting money from members of the public, including foreigners who did not carry their passports.
He urged the police to disclose the number of complaints received over such misconduct, as well as the number of officers investigated, prosecuted or dismissed.
He also asked whether there were officers who had refused to wear body cameras or deliberately switched them off while on duty. If so, he said, disciplinary action should be taken against them.

Lim urged the government to set a firm timeline for the full rollout of body cameras and establish clear procedures for storing recordings, controlling access to footage and penalising officers who tampered with evidence.
"Honest police officers should not be afraid of body cameras. The public is asked to respect the police, but the police must also prove that they deserve that respect," he said.
Last year, more than 7,000 body cameras were deployed across 157 police district headquarters and 640 police stations.
896e9c81df32d20d: PETALING JAYA: Marriage to an ethnic Malay Muslim does not automatically make a foreign spouse Malay, says home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

In a statement today, Saifuddin said a foreign national's ethnicity would remain unchanged after marrying a Malaysian of Malay descent, clarifying “misleading” reports on his written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
“I wish to emphasise that marriage between a Muslim foreign national and an ethnic Malay Malaysian does not change the foreign national's ethnicity to Malay.
“Their ethnicity remains unchanged, and the national registration department (JPN) will not determine the ethnicity of the foreign national concerned.

“This was clearly stated in my written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, but some reports used headlines that could cause misunderstanding and give the public a misleading impression of the matter.”
He urged the public to read beyond the headlines, check facts, and understand context before sharing information.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said children of Malay Muslims married to Muslim foreigners could be registered as Malays or according to the foreign parent's ancestry.
He was responding to Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis), who asked whether foreigners married to Malay Muslims could qualify as Bumiputeras and enjoy the associated rights and privileges.

Under the Constitution, a Malay is defined by criteria including professing Islam, habitually speaking the Malay language, conforming to Malay customs, and meeting the relevant constitutional requirements concerning birth or residence in the federation before Merdeka Day.

c4061952ea659375: Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom.

Honey bees (Apis mellifera) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee's stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed.
8636cf1c80924a2b: FRANKFURT: A flight from the Greek island of Corfu to Germany landed safely as planned in Nuremberg on Tuesday after a hijack alert issued from the cockpit that the airline put down to a "malfunction in the radio communication system".
Corendon Airlines said it wanted to "emphasise that no emergency situation occurred and that at no point were the passengers, flight crew or aircraft in any danger".
The incident forced a brief suspension of operations at Nuremberg Airport, where the plane was headed, the airport said. Flight operations later returned to normal.

"From the cockpit, the code '7500' (hijacking case) was transmitted, and furthermore, the pilot could no longer be reached by radio. For safety reasons, various alarm scrambles were then triggered," police earlier said on X.

The alert comes less than a month after the co-pilot of a jet bound for Israel from Dubai attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, with the United Arab Emirates' prosecutor general calling the incident a "terrorist attack".
The airline said the emergency code had been transmitted on Tuesday while the plane, a Boeing 737-800, was in Croatian airspace "due to a brief malfunction in the radio communication system".
"The situation was immediately monitored, investigations were promptly initiated and all necessary preparations were made. The aircraft landed safely at Nuremberg Airport," it said.
The airport said earlier on its website, "Flight operations are currently suspended due to an in-flight emergency. Flight XR 456 from Corfu to Nuremberg has since landed safely."
An airport spokesperson had no additional information.
A possible drone sighting had already disrupted air traffic at the airport overnight into Tuesday, the airport said in a separate statement.
German authorities have also been on heightened alert since a failed attack involving an explosives-laden drone at a German airport in August, which authorities blamed on Russia.
2d29b9b5a413b84c: LOS ANGELES, Oct 13 — Emergency repairs and cleanup were underway yesterday in California’s wave-battered city of Long Beach, where several homes appeared on the brink of collapse and remained too dangerous to enter.

Tropical Storm Rachel brought less rain than forecasters had predicted but the heavy surf — driven by a confluence of factors including the abnormal storm system, high tide, the impact of El Nino and human-caused climate change — was enough to severely damage some coastal properties.
Dramatic photos and video footage showed homes along the city’s peninsula teetering precariously, while its historic boardwalk was partially swept away.
“These kind of impacts are not normal. They’re unprecedented for our community,” said Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson during a weekend press conference.
“This is a sobering reminder of the power of nature,” he added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
An aerial view shows Pacific Ocean waves crashing into damaged homes amid high surf generated by Tropical Storm Rachel in Long Beach, California, on October 11, 2026. — AFP pic
Some residents who lived on particularly threatened blocks were issued mandatory evacuation orders through today.
Richardson urged people to take seriously warnings to prepare, including picking up city-provided sandbags, saying “our infrastructure was not built for this.”
“This accelerates all of our urgency to address climate resiliency on our coastline,” he added.
The local leader pointed to warnings that El Nino’s effects will worsen into the winter and are expected to wreak more havoc along California’s coast.

City official Tom Modica detailed a plan at the press conference for immediate and longer-term resiliency strategies, including repair of the damaged boardwalk as well as its failed bulkhead, a vertical retaining structure that’s meant to stabilise waterfront property.

Modica also pointed to a dredging project intended to widen the beach by about 200 feet (60 metres) by adding some 415,000 cubic yards (317,000 cubic metres) of sand, a project he said was now accelerated to begin October 19.

The National Hurricane Center said the worst of Rachel was over but “hazardous coastal conditions” could persist for days, with the highest waves coinciding with high tides, causing life-threatening surf and rip currents.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

An aerial view shows an emergency vehicle driving through coastal floodwaters amid strong waves and high tides generated by Tropical Storm Rachel in Newport Beach, California, on October 9, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Devastating’
Pacific hurricanes that impact southern California to this degree are rare.
Rachel was the latest named entrant in this year’s unusually active season, weather charged by the recurring El Nino pattern that this time around is particularly extreme.
El Nino raises surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean and causes global changes in winds and rainfall.
In the Atlantic, it tends to rein in the strength and frequency of hurricanes, but in the Pacific it has the opposite effect.
Human-caused climate change can worsen El Nino’s impacts.
A warmer atmosphere holds more moisture, allowing rains to turn more intense.
Paris Henken, a US competitive sailor, said in a viral Instagram post that she had been a tenant of one of the buildings now on the brink of collapse.

“An ocean front 1 bedroom that had everything we could have ever wanted. As an Olympic sailor aiming for LA2028 I was steps away from my playground (maybe a little too close),” she wrote in the caption.
“To see three storms undo a place that brought so much peace is devastating,” Henken continued.

She also referenced the chorus of criticism that many homes along California’s coast belong to the wealthy or are second homes, and that they never should’ve been built on such a vulnerable landscape.
“Although it’s true the Peninsula is home to many multi-million-dollar homes, our little community was far from that,” wrote the athlete.
“We are renters and can get up and move, but the sense of stability this apartment gave us was everything to me.” — AFP
1afaaef4df8a23d1: RIYADH, Oct 13 — Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, faces a major economic contraction this year, the IMF said today, as deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis squeeze a country already suffering from the Middle East war.

Saudi Arabia’s GDP is expected to shrink by 3.3 per cent, the International Monetary Fund said in its latest World Economic Outlook report, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockading of the Strait of Hormuz.

The report was compiled before 13 people were killed on Saturday — the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade — during a series of lethal Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s international airport.

The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on Hormuz, a vital shipping route for oil and gas, since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen civil war, pitting a Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government against the rival Houthis, has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.
Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi oil facilities, oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route — and transport hubs including airports.

Blasts resounded over the Saudi capital again late yesterday, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile and the group announcing it had once again targeted the airport, whose operations remain suspended.
In the evening, mobile phones received a government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat”, before the announcement of the interception.

Saturday’s airport attack prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.
Houthi warning
The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.
Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.
Riyadh’s coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, in a long-running civil war that has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.
In its latest global report, the IMF said the regional economy was projected to contract by 0.3 per cent this year, compared to its projected 1.9 per cent growth six months ago.
It cited “a longer closure of the Strait of Hormuz, compared with the baseline assumptions in the April” report, predicting a major rebound in 2027 based on the expected reopening of the waterway.

Since the Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran has sought to impose its control over the Strait of Hormuz, repeatedly attacking ships that transit without its authorisation.
The US has imposed its own counter-blockade on Iranian ports, and has escorted friendly ships through the waterway in increasing numbers.
The fund noted that Saudi Arabia is among the least affected exporters in the region, pointing to “an economy with more diversified export routes”.
Saudi Arabia has made use of its East-West oil pipeline to bypass the Hormuz strait and send crude to its Red Sea coast.
However, the pipeline was temporarily shut in September after it was hit by strikes blamed on Iran-backed groups in Iraq. — AFP
f7b05b7355693365: BANGKOK, Oct 13 — The IMF warned on Tuesday of “elevated” risks faced by the global financial system, with potential perils including an AI-related market correction and cyber threats that could have “severe” consequences.

The cautionary message was delivered by the International Monetary Fund’s latest Global Financial Stability Report, published on the second day of its annual gatherings with the World Bank, held this year in Thailand’s capital, Bangkok.
“These risks are plausible near-term catalysts for a sharp tightening of financial conditions and market turmoil,” the report said.

The recent boom in artificial intelligence — and the related rush to manufacture semiconductors and build data centres — has provided a boost to global growth despite geopolitical pressures including the Middle East war.
However, “growing evidence suggests that AI capabilities can be delivered at lower investment levels... or that potential economic gains may not be as large as expected,” the IMF warned.
“Weaker or less durable AI investments and profitability could be a shock that triggers a market correction.”
And while AI is increasingly a source of economic vitality globally, it is also presenting unprecedented risks, the Fund said.
“Severe cyber incidents could undermine market confidence and disrupt critical financial market infrastructure and operations,” it said.

The risks posed by cyber threats to the financial system are both “known and very much unknown”, Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director of the IMF’s Monetary and Capital Markets Department, told reporters after the report’s launch.
“The policy priority should be to strengthen resilience before new shocks hit the economy,” Vamvakidis said.
The report adds to growing worries about AI and its wide-ranging impact on labour markets, education and inequality.

In one widely covered incident in July, AI agents developed by US firm OpenAI hacked Hugging Face, an AI model and application library, as the autonomous software escaped its confined testing environment.
As AI capabilities continue to improve, the risk of successful cyberattacks on “critical financial institutions or market infrastructure” is getting “worse”, the IMF report said.
The “impact could be severe as rapid digitisation has increased the attack surface”.

Cyber threats are more menacing in emerging markets that have not allocated sufficient resources for prevention, Caio Ferreira, deputy division chief at the IMF’s Monetary and Capital Markets Department, said at the news conference.
While frontier AI models could be used to stage such attacks, they also have a role to play in cyber defence, the report said.
Another growing risk to the global financial system is a spike in bond yields, which could trigger severe shocks due to the “foundational importance of sovereign bond markets”, the report said.
“Bond markets are susceptible to further rises in energy prices reigniting inflation and forcing the tightening of monetary policy.” — AFP
49d8461c79eb546c: PARIS, Oct 13 — French high school pupils staged fresh nationwide rallies today urging better learning conditions, supported by university students and Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, with authorities and participants wary of further violence.

With just months to go before elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, French authorities had been hoping that the protests would start to ease ahead of half-term holidays to start at the end of the week.
But teenagers at high schools called lycees — backed by university students, teachers, unions and the far-left opposition France Unbowed party — have said their demands have not been met.
“They’re not listening to us, so we’re going to them,” university student union l’Union etudiante wrote on X.

Outside an art college in Paris, 19-year-old Gabin Jaze-Gaugain was among dozens of students striking peacefully in support of high school pupils, as police vans lined up on the other side of the boulevard.
“It’s a blockade in solidarity with the distress in public high schools in the suburbs and the rest of France,” he told AFP.
“High school kids have suffered great brutality,” he added after multiple allegations of police violence against protesters in recent weeks.
The student union reported 90 per cent of universities had closed nationwide to show support.

Thunberg, who became famous as a teen for school strikes to demand action on climate change, stood among pupils demonstrating outside a school at the heart of the movement in the capital’s largest suburb, Saint-Denis.
“Young people are not being included in the conversation. Our future is being robbed away from us,” the 23-year-old told reporters at the Paul Eluard high school.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Swedish activist Greta Thunberg looks on as she arrives to take part in a blockade at the Lycee Paul Eluard in Saint-Denis, on the outskirts of Paris on October 13, 2026, as part of a nationwide student mobilisation. — AFP pic
‘Just don’t get it’
French students say they are determined to press the government to address the problems of too many absent teachers, dilapidated buildings, overcrowded class schedules and other grievances.
The protests since last month have seen teenagers pile up dumpsters and security barriers outside hundreds of France’s 3,700 lycees.
The mobilisation was to include an early afternoon march through Paris, but rallies were already underway in other cities.
In the western city of Nantes, thousands marched behind a banner reading “Schools without money, a country without a future”.
“I think there are a lot of us in France who are still motivated,” 16-year-old Mariolino said.
“Those who think the anger will disappear with the holidays just don’t get it.”
In the northeastern city of Strasbourg, Adeline Ferier, 42, a middle school French teacher, said she was demonstrating to support her 16-year-old daughter.
“I think it’s great that young people are aware of inequalities and are getting involved,” she said.
More than 70,000 people took to the streets last Thursday in the last major event of a movement that sprang up in late September.
‘Issues that deserve time’
The demonstrations in recent weeks have mostly been peaceful, but clashes have occasionally broken out with police.
The education ministry said eight members of teaching staff were injured yesterday, mostly in the Paris region and the cities of Bordeaux and Lyon, in relation to the protests.
Authorities said fireworks fired through tubes injured two school workers in Reims, one school worker in a Paris suburb and a police officer outside a school in Marseille.
Today’s demonstrations supporting the students were to be followed on Saturday by wider public rallies against the rising cost of living.
Macron, speaking to reporters at a car show yesterday, urged restraint from protesters.
“These are issues that deserve time, consultations, discussion and respect,” Macron said just months before elections to replace him.
More than 6,800 people — largely minors — have been taken into police custody over the course of the protests, according to the justice ministry.
Police have opened internal investigations into 24 allegations of brutality against demonstrators.

After last week’s nationwide demonstrations, the government promised some 3,000 substitute teachers would be deployed in the coming days to replace absent staff at the 114 worst-affected high schools.
The education minister said today that 35 per cent had already been assigned.
High school students are demanding a €10 billion (US$11 billion) boost for lycees. — AFP
bf77bab08ac36e4a: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang Ahli Parlimen pembangkang mencadangkan kerajaan memberikan subsidi kepada perusahaan kecil selama tujuh bulan bagi membantu mereka membayar gaji pekerja mengikut kadar gaji minimum baharu RM2,000, berbanding mengecualikan mereka daripada kenaikan itu.

Ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat, Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) berkata skim itu akan dimulakan dengan 500,000 pekerja di perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS), dengan kerajaan menambah RM300 bagi setiap pekerja.
Pada kadar RM300 sebulan, beliau menganggarkan subsidi itu menelan belanja sehingga RM150 juta sebulan atau RM1.05 bilion bagi tempoh tujuh bulan, tidak termasuk kos pentadbiran.

Fadhli berkata pengecualian syarikat kecil daripada pelaksanaan gaji minimum baharu bermakna pekerja mereka terus menerima gaji RM1,700 sebulan, sedangkan pekerja di syarikat besar memperoleh RM2,000.
“Bagaimanapun, pengecualian ini tidak menyelesaikan masalah pokok. Sebaliknya, ia berisiko mewujudkan dua kumpulan pekerja dengan kadar gaji minimum yang berbeza,” katanya.
“Ini memberi kesan buruk kepada pekerjaan. Ia boleh menyebabkan pekerja mahir berpindah ke syarikat besar, sekali gus menyukarkan PMKS mengekalkan pekerja dan akhirnya menjejaskan daya saing mereka.”
Bagi membiayai subsidi itu, Fadhli mencadangkan peruntukan RM3.8 juta bagi setiap Ahli Parlimen kerajaan pada 2027 dipotong, yang menurutnya boleh menjimatkan RM581.4 juta.
“Daripada langkah itu sahaja, kita boleh menjimatkan lebih setengah bilion ringgit daripada peruntukan yang diberikan kepada Ahli Parlimen kerajaan,” dakwanya.

Beliau berkata baki dana boleh diperoleh melalui pemotongan perbelanjaan kerajaan yang lain, termasuk peruntukan Jabatan Perdana Menteri (JPM) yang menurutnya meningkat daripada RM10 bilion kepada RM11.6 bilion.
Di bawah Belanjawan 2027, gaji minimum akan dinaikkan daripada RM1,700 kepada RM2,000 mulai Jun depan, namun perniagaan dengan jualan tahunan di bawah RM50 juta akan dikecualikan.
Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin semalam turut membangkitkan kebimbangan sama dengan memberi amaran bahawa pengecualian itu akan mewujudkan gaji berbeza dalam kalangan pekerja.
d01ed950c6cc2459: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has become the latest financial heavyweight to warn that the AI spending frenzy could end in tears, with consequences extending well beyond the tech sector. In its latest Global Financial Stability Report, published on Tuesday, the IMF warns that financial markets are increasingly exposed to an AI-driven correction, especially if the billions poured into the tech fail to deliver the profits investors expect. AI investment has helped keep markets and economic growth ticking along, but the IMF fears the boom could quickly turn to bust if the promised profits fail to materialize. With tech giants borrowing billions and investors piling into the same handful of companies, a selloff could leave more than just Silicon Valley nursing a hangover. The watchdog is also concerned about circular financing arrangements, in which AI firms act as one another's investors, financiers, and customers. These deals might help keep the AI money machine running, but they also mean financial trouble at one company could quickly become somebody else's problem. The IMF isn't the only one getting nervous. Jefferies strategist Chris Wood has warned that America's AI spending spree could cause "massive capital destruction," with cheaper Chinese open source models threatening the returns US tech giants are counting on. The warning also follows similar concerns raised by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), which cautioned in June that the AI boom had uncomfortable similarities to previous financial bubbles. With so much money tied up in a relatively small number of tech companies, it warned that a sudden loss of investor confidence could send shockwaves through global financial markets. As if the prospect of an AI-fueled market meltdown weren't enough, the IMF has identified two other threats to financial stability: rising government bond yields and cyberattacks. Higher yields could increase borrowing costs for governments already struggling with debt, while the latter could bring critical financial services to a grinding halt. Banks have become increasingly reliant on the same handful of cloud providers and software suppliers, creating shared points of failure that could spread disruption across institutions. If a cyberattack took down a major bank or critical tech provider, the IMF warns the fallout could disrupt everything from payments and trading to customers accessing their deposits. Software vendors aren't getting much of a head start either. According to the IMF, more than 70 percent of tracked vulnerabilities exploited so far in 2026 were already being abused by attackers before or on the day they were publicly disclosed, underscoring how little warning defenders may receive. AI could make matters worse here too, as the IMF warns that increasingly capable models are giving cybercriminals more powerful tools, potentially making it easier to find and exploit vulnerabilities at speed. Despite the gloomy outlook, the IMF isn't predicting an imminent financial collapse. It says global financial markets have remained resilient, and its stress testing suggests the banking system could withstand a severe downturn, although weaker institutions would be more exposed. Still, the watchdog wants regulators to keep a closer eye on excessive borrowing, concentrated investments, and cyber resilience before any of these risks turn into a full-blown crisis. For an industry promising to revolutionize the global economy, accidentally helping to crash it would be quite the plot twist.®
1c85cb0ceb47cf2c: BANGKOK: EU economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis told AFP on Tuesday that Russian diesel sales recently authorised by the US were unlikely to move the price of the commodity, which has spiked since the start of the Iran war.

US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that he had spoken to President Vladimir Putin and they had struck an agreement for Russia to release large amounts of diesel onto world markets, a bid to lower prices that have spiked since the US leader launched the war on Iran on Feb 28.

"As regards specifically this question on Russian diesel exports, if we look at the volumes, they are not of any macroeconomic significance, and frankly, there are strong doubts whether Russia is even able to supply those volumes, and according also to US quality standards, those are big question marks," Dombrovskis said in an exclusive interview with AFP on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

He said the EU would be approaching international partners to step up financial support for Ukraine during the week of meetings in the Thai capital, which brings together finance ministers, central bank governors and other top officials from around the globe.

Dombrovskis addressed a range of topics, including spiking sovereign bond yields in Europe, concerns around inflation due to rising energy prices and a recently concluded trade deal with China under which Beijing agreed to cap hybrid car exports to the 27-nation bloc.
"If we look at the broader EU-China trade relations, last year we were having around a €360 billion trade deficit, meaning like almost €1 billion per day," he said.

"So obviously, that's very unbalanced relations. That's not sustainable. So here we are discussing specifically automotive, but we need this rebalancing across, I would say, a broader range of sectors," Dombrovskis said.
The EU will cap imports of hybrid vehicles from China to 350,000 a year, a senior EU official said on Monday, after Brussels and Beijing agreed to the limit in a bid to avert a trade war.
The cap will apply from 2027 for a period of four years and will rise by six percent annually from the second year onwards.
'Prolonged uncertainty'

Addressing spiking sovereign bond yields, especially in France, the EU economy chief said it was important for Paris to pass its recently shared "ambitious draft budget" in order to address uncertainty risks.
The yield on 10-year French government bonds is now flirting with the psychological threshold of five percent, a level not seen since 2002, after weeks of heavy selling.
"Prolonged uncertainty is going to negatively impact those yields, so therefore it's important to have clarity about the budget," he said.
France is considered a core eurozone economy, with investors usually seeing its sovereign debt as among the most trustworthy.
However, since the massive stimulus spending during the Covid pandemic, officials have failed to reduce the resulting debt pile amid anaemic economic growth.
Dombrovskis said the average maturity of French sovereign debt was quite long, so the process of debt servicing costs rising would be gradual.
He did not see the issue as being a risk to financial stability for the time being.
"Euro Area member states have time, but they need to do necessary adjustments. They need to make sure that they have sustainable public finances," he said.

3279f7c79a7c7cf1: OCTOBER 13 — The ultimate measure of the success of Budget 2027 is not so much in macro-economic figures but in the tangible impact felt on the ground by businesses and workers.
In Budget 2027 the Madani government has dubbed 2027 officially as the Year of Malaysian MSMEs.

MSMEs are often cited as the backbone of the economy making up 97.4 per cent of all businesses in Malaysia with microenterprises taking up 77.4 per cent, small-sized firms 21.4 per cent and medium-sized firms 1.1 per cent. They employ 8.1 million people or 48.7 per cent of the total workforce.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

File photo of store workers and customers around Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman in Kuala Lumpur. MSMEs are often cited as the backbone of the economy making up 97.4 per cent of all businesses in Malaysia with microenterprises taking up 77.4 per cent, small-sized firms 21.4 per cent and medium-sized firms 1.1 per cent. — Picture by Shafwan Zaidon

In 2025, MSMEs outpaced national GDP growth with value-added growing by 5.7 per cent and exceeding the overall national GDP growth rate of 5.2 per cent. MSMEs accounted for 39.7 per cent of Malaysia’s total GDP.

Services and manufacturing have a combined share of 84.5 per cent of MSME GDP, with agriculture (8.4 per cent), construction (5.3 per cent) and mining and quarrying (0.5 per cent) making up the balance.

MSME exports expanded by 10.5 per cent to RM214.5 billion driven by manufacturing exports up 8.8 per cent and services exports up 14.0 per cent, accounting for 14.7 per cent of Malaysia’s total exports.
MSME labour productivity rose by 4.1 per cent led by strong gains in construction up 10.8 per cent and manufacturing up 4.8 per cent.

At the helm of this transformation is Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister Steven Sim. The sweeping measures unveiled under his ministry are more than just a policy package; they are a ground-up reform.

They are further evidence that Sim is bringing precisely the same hands-on, proactive leadership to the Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) that he previously demonstrated during his widely praised tenure at the Ministry of Human Resources.

True to his reputation for stakeholder engagement, Sim and the Madani government have structured Budget 2027 around three core pillars: easing financing access, reducing business costs, and opening up broader market opportunities.

Under Kuskop’s strategic ABCD framework, encompassing Productivity Shift (Anjakan Produktiviti), Simplified Bureaucracy (Birokrasi Dipermudah), Capital Access (Capaian Modal), and Market Accessibility (Daya Akses Pasaran), the policy interventions are both targeted and pragmatic.
Loan and financing guarantees for businesses, including MSMEs and mid-tier companies, have reached a historic high of RM57 billion, up from RM50 billion in 2026.
This includes RM6.6 billion in micro-financing through institutions like AIM, TEKUN, and BSN, alongside RM32 billion in financing guarantees via SJPP and CGC.

Recognising the tight margins faced by smaller businesses, corporate income taxes for MSMEs have been reduced by up to two per cent, giving up to RM6,000 a year in savings for roughly 300,000 businesses.

Practical bureaucratic relief is also available for small traders. Those renting DBKL premises will benefit from a 50 per cent rental discount throughout 2027, while government procurement processes have been streamlined through direct appointments of up to RM200,000 for eligible maintenance and repair works.

Rather than imposing blanket regulations that choke small enterprises, Sim has championed calibrated relief, such as shielding smaller enterprises from sudden operational strains while actively injecting RM30 million to help 4,000 MSMEs harness AI and automation.

Initiatives like matching grants for first-time halal certification and an expanded RM7.5 billion in procurement opportunities for Bumiputera G1 to G4 contractors demonstrate a holistic “whole-of-government” approach that leaves no entrepreneur behind.

By weaving together a robust RM1.028 billion allocation for Kuskop, targeted export funding via BPMB and Matrade, and a firm eye on fair digital trade through the proposed E-Commerce Bill, Budget 2027 lays down a resilient foundation for Malaysia’s economic future.
In times of global uncertainty, effective leadership is marked by clarity of vision and genuine care for the rakyat.
Under Steven Sim’s stewardship, Kuskop is proving that economic growth and social compassion are not mutually exclusive — they are the twin engines driving Malaysia forward.

5c0b17682845c984: Cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems reportedly pushed temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F), affecting hundreds of stores in France and forcing retailers to discard food. Major supermarkets such as Carrefour, Coopérative U, Intermarché, Monoprix, and more were hit by the attacks, which spoiled perishable food and left stores without fresh produce. The affected equipment includes cold-storage units used to hold food before it reaches supermarket shelves. The criminals behind the attack raised temperatures to unsafe levels, spoiling food and in some cases starting fires. Some affected retailers used refrigeration controllers produced by Danish company Danfoss. Authorities have not identified the entry point or confirmed exploitation of the vulnerabilities previously disclosed by Claroty and patched in August 2025, although the manufacturer said affected stores were running outdated firmware. Experts say the previously identified vulnerabilities were easily scriptable and relied on a unique but predictable authentication method. Claroty found a hidden authentication mechanism in the AK-SM 800A platform that accepted a code generated from the device's current date, bypassing the configured administrator password. Anyone who reproduced the algorithm could generate a valid daily code and gain administrative access. "It's a zero-skill thing to pull off, I wrote the bash script while having a shit," said security pro Kevin Beaumont. The research demonstrated how compromised controllers could expose refrigeration systems to physical disruption, although the vulnerabilities' role in this week's attacks remains unconfirmed. Danfoss told reporters this week that the French supermarkets affected by the attacks "were running outdated firmware" and that the company has consistently advocated for keeping systems updated. The Register asked Danfoss if it would confirm whether the previously disclosed bugs were exploited to execute the attacks, and whether the same bug was also abused in August to compromise US military commissary refrigerators, which led to food losses. CERT-FR published an alert reporting numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, which were not mentioned in Claroty's original reporting nor in Danfoss's advisories at the time. The authority advised disconnecting or restricting network access. For suspected compromises, it recommended a factory reset, security patches, credential rotation, account checks, and full reconfiguration. For those wondering why fridges even need to be reachable via the internet, the main reason is that it allows central engineering teams to troubleshoot issues remotely, according to Claroty's researchers. "Industrial control systems such as refrigeration controllers are often assumed to be on safely isolated networks. However, our research found many of these devices are directly exposed to the public internet," said Amir Preminger, CTO at Claroty. "While this convenience significantly reduces maintenance costs by allowing engineers to troubleshoot issues remotely, it also lowers the barrier to entry for attackers. "Organizations must take proactive measures to ensure that management interfaces are not insecurely connected to the internet, and ensure that access to administrative services is restricted to trusted management networks or secured through VPNs and other appropriate network segmentation controls." Intermarché owner Groupement Les Mousquetaires said around 150 of its supermarkets were affected by the attacks, while Carrefour confirmed around 80 impacted stores. Monoprix said roughly 5 percent of its 490 stores were experiencing the same issues, and Coopérative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said 80 of the company’s 2,000 stores were hit, adding that the attack on the food sector was “unacceptable.” “Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products is an attack on the French food supply chain,” he said. “It is unprecedented, extremely serious, and unacceptable. We remain fully mobilized.” However, in a separate twist, Schelcher told French radio station RTL on Tuesday that Coopérative U is not a customer of Danfoss. The Register contacted Coopérative U for more information about what caused the attacks at its stores. Shodan searches for internet-facing Danfoss controller interfaces indicated that more than 4,500 endpoints were exposed as of Monday, with more than half of those located in France. Ahold Delhaize, a major grocery retailer in the Netherlands, announced on the same day that it was experiencing a "security issue." No link to the refrigeration attacks in France has been established. The end result is similar, however, as the company's grocery brands are reporting stock issues. Several of the group's brands have taken their websites offline and posted notices about the "cybersecurity incident." Stores remain open, but affected brands have reported disruption to websites, apps, customer services, and online deliveries. The disruption hit the company's distribution systems, although these are now being restored. Updates posted to social media on Tuesday told shoppers that staff were once again able to use digital shelf labels but stock levels may vary across stores, and long-life items were likely to be more abundant than fresh fruit and vegetables. The retailer previously suffered a cyberattack in November 2024 that disrupted its US operations. ®

e0bcdbcf2c805a9d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said.
He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month.
“However, I want to emphasise that changes in weather conditions alone are not a long-term solution to the haze issue. It could happen again.

“Fire prevention efforts must therefore address the problem at its source. Domestic enforcement must be strengthened, while regional cooperation must be enhanced to reduce the risk of similar incidents recurring,” he said during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.
The issue was also raised by Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) and Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong).

Yii said the haze was no longer merely a seasonal nuisance but an annual emergency requiring stronger action, including the proposed introduction of a Cross-Border Haze Pollution Act and greater transparency in sharing hotspot data and information on plantation concessions.
Young Syefura, meanwhile, sought clarification on the government’s diplomatic engagements with Indonesia, including the responses received and the effectiveness of the measures taken.
She also called for stronger domestic enforcement and better protection for vulnerable groups.

In his response, Syed Ibrahim said the latest haze episode was caused by an increase in forest and land fires in several parts of Indonesia, including Kalimantan and Sumatra, which had affected air quality in Malaysia, particularly in Sarawak.
He said the Department of Environment (DOE) received 2,104 complaints concerning open burning and carried out 3,039 enforcement actions between August 3 and October 9.
These comprised 2,104 monitoring actions, 168 field orders, 32 notices, 13 compounds and two court actions.

As part of the mitigation efforts, the government also conducted 11 cloud seeding operations between August 30 and October 15 in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the National Disaster Management Agency and the Malaysian Army.
“The main challenge in enforcing laws with cross-border elements is obtaining sufficient evidence to establish the source of pollution and identify the parties responsible,” he said.

Syed Ibrahim added that the ministry had yet to receive any official information from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities regarding the alleged involvement of Malaysian companies in open-burning incidents in Indonesia. — Bernama

deaf33d2cdf62843: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan.

7d8bcea5a782ef7a: PETALING JAYA, Oct 13 — A businessman was sentenced to six months’ jail by the Magistrate’s Court here today for assaulting his former girlfriend, causing injuries to her eyes and body, two years ago.
Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case.

“The court orders that the prison sentence take effect from the date of conviction today. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said.
The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.
However, the court allowed an application by defence counsel Cheow Wee to stay the prison sentence pending an appeal to the High Court, but ordered that the compensation be paid today.
Hoh was charged with intentionally causing hurt to Liaw Ju Shuang, 28, at a residence in Putra Permai Town Centre, Seri Kembangan, at 12.30am on October 5, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.

In her judgment, Amira Sariaty said that although the neighbour, the third prosecution witness, did not witness the assault, the witness saw the victim with a bleeding head and bruises around her eyes and other parts of her body when she sought help.
“The witness also contacted the police, who took the victim to hospital for treatment. There was no reason for the victim to fabricate a story to frame the accused.

“In view of this, the court finds that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against the prosecution’s case, and was merely a denial unsupported by strong evidence and testimony,” Amira Sariaty said.
During mitigation, the defence sought a fine, citing the accused’s eyesight problems, which it said would make imprisonment difficult for him.

However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Syed Ahmed Khabir Abdul Rahman sought a jail term and a fine, arguing that the public interest outweighed that of the accused, given the extent of the victim’s injuries, and requested that compensation be awarded to her. — Bernama
b4b12e6b080ca46d: A person claiming responsibility for the breach of Denmark's Central Register of Persons (CPR) says they gained access through an IT company's account protected by the password "123456." The person told Danish news outlet Politiken they had no intention of selling or leaking the data. The newspaper reported that at least three company accounts, including an administrator account, used the same password. Denmark's CPR administration confirmed a breach affecting the information belonging to 8.8 million people on October 5, adding that a Danish company's legal access to the CPR system was abused. It did not name Funen-based Pays ApS as the company in question, but managing director Sophie Laursen confirmed on October 9 that it's access had been exploited. Pays' website has been taken offline, and the business has not responded to The Register's request for more information about the password claims. Pays had authorized access to the CPR system to provide services such as validating business customers' records. The Danish government says information relating to 8.8 million people was accessed. The register contains approximately 11 million records, including those of deceased people and people who have moved abroad. The government did not respond to questions about the alleged password failings. According to documents obtained by broadcaster TV 2, the attacker gained access to the CPR system on September 10 and ran the 14 million automated searches between then and September 20. The intrusion was detected on October 2, 12 days after the last reported searches. Mikkel Leihardt, director of the government's higher education and science ministry, told reporters at a press conference that the attack was discovered after a department staffer picked up an invoice indicating unusually high activity from Pays. The Danish data protection authority, Datatilsynet, was notified on October 4, and the government disclosed the attack the following day. ®
1d837fc0240650a9: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz.

“If you look at it objectively, it is a well-thought-out and balanced budget that takes into account the interests of all stakeholders while ensuring that both the lower- and higher-income groups are supported,” he said.

552d57189da3762a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Badminton Association of Malaysia (BAM) hopes that the Sports Matching Grant (GPS) announced in Budget 2027 will continue to assist the sport’s governing body as well as other sports associations.

4dc5ab98c5a371a5: Datacenters are forecast to consume a growing share of Europe's electricity by 2035, potentially pushing up consumer prices and prompting governments to impose price caps or restrictions on bit barns, according to Moody's. The credit rating agency is keeping tabs on the financial implications for datacenter operators and electricity networks. It predicts that while power consumption by server farms is relatively modest today, these facilities are set to become major drivers of electricity demand by 2035, requiring utilities and network operators to invest in generation and grid capacity. Massive compute sheds still accounted for "a low single-digit share" of electricity in most of the largest European markets in 2025, typically about 2.5 percent. But some of the major markets such as the UK and France are set to see accelerating growth in the number and size of facilities that could substantially increase their share of electricity consumption. The report estimates datacenters will account for at least 5.7 percent of electricity demand in France and the UK by 2035, but could be as high as 17 percent for the Netherlands and 30 percent for Ireland. The latter country is regarded as an outlier, however, as datacenters already made up 23 percent of Ireland's electricity consumption in 2025 – up from just 5 percent in 2015. In addition, the EU has set out the goal of more than tripling the bloc's datacenter capacity within five to seven years, and wants to diversify where such projects are sited beyond the primary markets such as Germany, Ireland, France, and the Netherlands to secondary markets in the Nordics and southern Europe. This means more power generation will be needed, plus expansion of the grid networks to carry the extra energy to where it is required. Moody's says this has the potential to put pressure on grid operators' balance sheets in the short term, compounded by the lag in recovering higher capital spending under many European regulatory regimes. This pressure is more pronounced for transmission networks than distribution networks because datacenter operators are required to fund only the cost of the connection to the grid, the report by Moody's notes. It highlights some novel approaches adopted by utilities, such as repurposing old fossil-fuel plant sites for server farm projects because of their existing grid connections – as is said to be the case with at least one of the UK government's AI Growth Zones – and partnering with developers to build new facilities and supply them with power. The cost of expanding power grids, together with supply-demand imbalances, is set to push energy prices higher, Moody's forecasts. Historically, this has prompted political measures to limit the financial burden borne by customers, it says. Some governments are already considering tax cuts and additional subsidies for end users, while a growing number of transmission networks are starting to demand financial guarantees to screen out speculative or duplicative projects. The UK government is mulling over this measure, as we reported during the summer. Looking ahead, intervention could become more intrusive through measures such as electricity price caps, additional taxes, or levies. Moody's cites Ireland as an example, where the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU) replaced a moratorium on new datacenter grid connections with a framework under which operators applying for a grid connection rated at 10 MVA or more must provide matching power generation or storage capacity on-site or nearby, and meet at least 80 percent of their annual electricity demand through additional renewable projects in Ireland. In America, President Trump brought in a Ratepayer Protection Pledge to try to defuse growing voter unhappiness at datacenters and their effects on energy bills. The pledge now covers utility companies, bit barn developers, and state governments with a pinky promise that citizens' bills won't rise to pay for all the extra energy and grid infrastructure needed. Moody's expects more European governments to follow the US and Ireland in intervening over datacenter power demand if expansion continues on its current trajectory. ®

78bbb2bc867be9d5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Better school facilities, improved safety and a more conducive learning environment are among the key improvements the school community hopes to see from the increased allocation for education in Budget 2027.

West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students.

Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.

On the Supplementary Food Programme (RMT), he said its implementation must be closely monitored to ensure students received meals that met the required quality standards and complied with the prescribed menu and portion sizes.

Meanwhile, Federation of Peninsular Malay Students (GPMS) president Muhd Fazreen Ismadi Fauzi said increasing the Early Schooling Assistance (BAP) to RM200 would help parents, particularly those from the B40 group, meet the cost of preparing their children for school.

On the RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students, Muhd Fazreen suggested that the aid be disbursed monthly rather than in a lump sum, allowing students to manage their educational expenses more effectively throughout the year.

“For GPMS, it would be better to pay the allowance monthly rather than in one lump sum. If students receive the full amount at once, they might spend it in a day on things like mobile phones, and the money may not last them through the year,” he said.

Muhd Fazreen also stressed the need to ensure school facilities cater to students with disabilities, particularly with the planned enrolment of six-year-olds in Year One from 2027.
He said schools must be equipped with suitable facilities and support services to meet the needs of all students. — Bernama
c1e8459dce0baf95: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations.

He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives.

“I will discuss with National Unity Minister (Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang) to identify the most appropriate steps. If possible, we will work towards organising something in conjunction with National Month celebrations next year.”
Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) editor-in-chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj, Daily Express chief editor Datuk Sardahthisa James and Victor’s son Benedict Morais.

Fahmi said the collection highlighted the importance of preserving the intellectual contributions and perspectives of the country’s founding figures, particularly at a time when rapid development and the pursuit of future progress could overshadow an understanding of the nation’s past.
The communications minister said the book deserved wider circulation beyond its initial print run of 2,000 copies to ensure its valuable historical content reached a broader audience.

In this regard, Fahmi offered to help raise funds to print an additional 2,000 copies, subject to the agreement of those involved in the publication, and proposed organising a related programme at Parliament next year.
He said he would distribute copies to all Cabinet ministers at Friday’s meeting to highlight the importance of understanding Malaysia’s nation-building history.

Meanwhile, Sardahthisa, also known as James Sarda, said the book provided valuable insights into the aspirations of Malaysia’s founding leaders and the challenges they faced during the country’s formation, making it an important resource for researchers, policymakers and younger generations.
He collaborated with Benedict to republish the collection, originally released in 1967 under the title Selected Speeches.

“For journalists like me, finding speeches delivered by Tunku Abdul Rahman and Tun Abdul Razak in Parliament is not easy, as record-keeping was different in those days and access to parliamentary records involved various protocols.
“This book is a gold mine for research. It is a one-stop centre containing the speeches of leaders from various backgrounds and their hopes for Malaysia,” he told reporters after the event.

Meanwhile, Benedict recalled that his father was a self-taught journalist who honed his skills through a correspondence course at Rapid Results College (RRC) in London at a time when formal journalism training was not widely available.
The 80-year-old said his father later gained practical experience through on-the-job training, reflecting the determination and initiative that shaped his career in journalism.

Recalling the declaration of independence on Aug 31, 1957, Benedict said he was a 12-year-old student among the 25,000 people who witnessed the historic occasion at Merdeka Stadium, including Tunku Abdul Rahman’s seven resounding cries of “Merdeka”.
He also recalled the strong sense of unity among the people during that period, when they simply identified themselves as Malayans regardless of race.

“We saw ourselves as Malayans…neighbours kept their homes open, shared food and visited one another freely. It was a spirit of unity that came naturally rather than being imposed,” he added. — Bernama
